stories.title: Knicks blow by the Cavaliers in the fourth, win 121-102 for sixth straight victory
stories.summary: — Jose Alvarado scored a season-high 21 points, Mikal Bridges had a season-best 19 and the New York Knicks rode a blitz by their bench to a 121-102 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Wednesday night that extended their winning streak to six.
stories.detailText: NEW YORK -- — Jose Alvarado scored a season-high 21 points, Mikal Bridges had a season-best 19 and the New York Knicks rode a blitz by their bench to a 121-102 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Wednesday night that extended their winning streak to six. Jalen Brunson also scored 19, but the Knicks captain, who was questionable earlier in the day with an illness, labored to a 6-for-22 shooting night and the Knicks fell behind by 11 points multiple times. It was Alvarado, his backup, who was on the floor when the Knicks blew by the Cavaliers to start the fourth quarter. Josh Hart had 15 points, 12 assists and seven rebounds, and Karl-Anthony Towns finished with 12 points, 10 rebounds and seven assists, barely extending his season-opening streak to 17 consecutive games with a double-double. The defending champion Knicks would have been eliminated from NBA Cup title contention with a loss but outscored the Cavs 39-17 in the fourth on their blue court with orange lining the outside. Donovan Mitchell scored 30 points and James Harden had 28 for the Cavaliers, who fell to 9-10. Both teams were without their top defensive forwards, with the Knicks' OG Anunoby sidelined by a strained left calf and Cleveland's Evan Mobley still out with a toe injury. New York was also without key reserves Deuce McBride (left adductor tightness) and Jordan Clarkson (right plantar fasciitis), and lost backup center Andre Drummond to a head injury during the game. The Cavaliers led by 11 with under four minutes remaining in the first half. They went back ahead by 11 in the third quarter but the Knicks had it down to 85-82 headed to the fourth, then surged into the lead when Alvarado made consecutive 3-pointers for a 90-85 lead. Pacome Dadiet , another backup, then had consecutive baskets on the break, and after a Cleveland 3-pointer, Bridges scored and Alvarado made another 3 and suddenly it was the Knicks with an 11-point lead. When third-string center James Wiseman had consecutive baskets, the Knicks had outscored the Cavs 25-9 to start the fourth and had a 107-94 lead. Up next Cavaliers: Host Miami on Sunday. Knicks: Host Miami on Friday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

stories.title: Cavs suffer familiar loss to Knicks; Mitchell’s 30 points not enough
stories.summary: The Cavs fall to 2-2 in the NBA Cup.
stories.detailText: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 25: Donovan Mitchell #45 of the Cleveland Cavaliers controls the ball as Landry Shamet #44 of the New York Knicks defends during the first half in a the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup at Madison Square Garden on November 25, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Cavaliers have all but been eliminated from the NBA Cup after the New York Knicks, who outscored them 39-17 in the fourth quarter to pick up their second win over Cleveland this season. The Cavs are now 2-2 in the cup, making it almost certain they will miss out on advancing to the next stage. There’s always next year. Cleveland’s defensive focus and energy were much improved in the first half compared to their previous loss in Chicago. The Cavs played on a string, trusting each other by not overhelping — while seamlessly communicating through switches and containing New York’s off-ball screening actions by working together. Donovan Mitchell was relentlessly getting downhill throughout the first half. Mitchell opened the game shooting 8-for-9 from inside two-point range. He entered halftime with 20 points. James Harden chipped in with 14 points on 8-for-8 shooting from the free-throw line in the first half. Mikal Bridges led the Knicks with 17 points on 8-of-11 shooting overall. The Cavs hit the ground running in the third quarter, controlling the tempo and putting New York on the back foot before a myriad of fouls slowed the game to a crawl. This abrupt shift allowed the Knicks to storm back and make the game competitive again. Cleveland found themselves trailing by double digits in the fourth quarter as the Knicks began turning defense into offense. A handful of errant turnovers from the Cavs’ backcourt fueled the run. Winning the possession battle has been an emphasis for the Cavs, especially in this matchup. The Knicks have historically punished Cleveland by grabbing offensive rebounds and making it impossible to end defensive possessions. The Cavs started off on the right foot in that regard. They were outscoring New York 11-to-1 on second-chance points and had full control of the possession battle. But then it all fell apart. The Knicks grabbed every key rebound, forced backbreaking turnovers, and hit all of the big shots down the stretch to put this game out of reach. A fate the Cavs have suffered more than once to this team. As stated, it was a 22-point bludgeoning in the fourth quarter that closed the door. Harden and Mitchell combined for 58 points. Both struggled in the fourth quarter after playing stellar basketball before. Their six shared turnovers felt like they came at the worst times. The Cavs end the night officially below .500 with a 9-10 record. Not how anyone hoped this season would start.

stories.title: Knicks assistant coach Chris Jent returns to team
stories.summary: Chris Jent was back on New York's bench for Wednesday night's NBA Cup win against Cleveland after a monthlong absence.
stories.detailText: NEW YORK -- Knicks assistant coach Chris Jent returned to the team Wednesday following a leave of absence . Jent stepped away from the Knicks in late October for an undisclosed reason, shortly after the season began. He was back on the bench for Wednesday night's 121-102 NBA Cup win against the Cleveland Cavaliers . Jent, 56, was a member of Knicks head coach Mike Brown's staff in Cleveland and was on the Charlotte Hornets ' coaching staff in 2024-25. He was the Orlando Magic 's interim coach for 18 games in 2004-05. Jent played at Ohio State from 1988 to 1992.

stories.title: 76ers' Jaylen Brown exits with recurrence of hamstring issue
stories.summary: Jaylen Brown exited Philadelphia's NBA Cup game Wednesday night against Miami and was ruled out because of left hamstring tightness.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- 76ers forward Jaylen Brown exited Wednesday night's 111-104 NBA Cup win against the Miami Heat and was ruled out because of left hamstring tightness. Coach Nick Nurse said postgame that Brown would undergo imaging and the team would have an update on his hamstring Thursday. After scoring his sixth point of the night on a step-back jump shot late in the second quarter, Brown immediately shook his head and grabbed the hamstring, then signaled to the Sixers bench that he needed to check out of the game. The injury started for Brown in last week's win over the Brooklyn Nets in which he tied his season high of 31 points. Brown left that game early because of a hamstring strain and missed the Sixers' next two wins over the Orlando Magic and Milwaukee Bucks . He returned in Monday's loss to the Portland Trail Blazers , scoring 20 points. After that game, Brown said he had "a little bit of soreness." "You want to make sure you play it the right way, be safe," he said. "Also, don't want to miss a lot of games, so I want to be out there, but also got to be smart. So I think I played it the right way today." Brown is averaging 22.4 points, 6.3 rebounds and 3.6 assists on the season. The Sixers play at the Indiana Pacers on Friday. Center Joel Embiid missed Wednesday's game and the loss to the Blazers because of an illness.

stories.title: Matas Buzelis scores 24 as Bulls hold on to beat Hornets 107-105 for 2nd straight win
stories.summary: — Matas Buzelis scored 24 points, Josh Giddey added 12 points, 11 rebounds and seven assists, and the Chicago Bulls handed the Charlotte Hornets their seventh straight loss 107-105 on Wednesday night.
stories.detailText: CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- — Matas Buzelis scored 24 points, Josh Giddey added 12 points, 11 rebounds and seven assists, and the Chicago Bulls handed the Charlotte Hornets their seventh straight loss 107-105 on Wednesday night. Tre Jones had 10 points and eight assists for the Bulls, who escaped with their second straight win when Coby White’s off-balance jumper rimmed out at the buzzer. Brandon Miller led the Hornets with 35 points, his fourth 30-point game of the season. Naz Reid had 18 points, while Moussa Diabate added 14 points and 14 rebounds for the Hornets, who shot 41% from the field. The game featured 22 lead changes, more than half of those in the fourth quarter. With the Bulls leading by one, Buzelis tipped in a weakside rebound with 23.2 seconds left to make it a 3-point game. Miller scored on a driving layup with 18.7 seconds left to cut the lead back to one, but Buzelis answered with two free throws with 10.1 seconds left to push the lead back to three. The Hornets wanted a 3 to tie, but Buzelis fouled White on the floor before he could get a shot off. White made two free throws with 8.8 seconds left to cut the lead back to one. White dove on the floor to deny a side inbounds pass on Chicago's next possession, but was whistled for a foul. Jones missed the first of two free throws with 8.5 seconds left but made the second. Without any timeouts left, the Hornets inbounded the ball and White drove the length of the floor before launching a leaning 15-foot jumper from the right side that missed. The Bulls wrapped up NBA group play with a 2-2 record, while the Hornets finished 0-4. Charlotte led 48-46 at halftime despite shooting 36% from the field and 21% from beyond the arc. Up next Bulls: Host Pacers on Saturday night. Hornets: Host Nets on Saturday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

stories.title: NBA trade rumors 2026-27: Will Anthony Davis get traded? Clippers as sellers.
stories.summary: A little Thanksgiving appetizer of NBA trade rumors.
stories.detailText: For Thanksgiving, here is, if not a feast, at least an appetizer of NBA trade rumors as we move toward the end of the month. Will Anthony Davis get traded? The answer depends on who you ask. As league sources from other teams have told NBC Sports, they expect Washington to at least entertain offers from other teams — the Wizards need to build long-term around AJ Dybantsa and Davis would bring back a haul (while Trae Young has the most untradable contract in the league right now. However, it's no lock Davis will end up on the market, reports Jake Fischer of The Stein Line . Davis isn't pushing for it, he's playing at a high level, and if the Wizards look like a playoff team they may not be looking to deal, even though he can be a free agent next summer (Davis has a $62.8 million player option and has said he doesn't want to talk extension during the season). If Davis becomes available, keep an eye on the Toronto Raptors, Golden State Warriors and Atlanta Hawks, Fischer adds. Maybe this is all posturing by the Wizards. Either way, what is clear is that this conversation is happening close to the trade deadline, not before. Clippers expected to be sellers While the parents are away — owner Steve Ballmer and head of basketball operations Lawrence Frank are suspended — GM Trent Redden will play. Multiple reports say the Clippers are expected to be sellers at the deadline, most recently from Jake Fischer of The Stein Line . LA is willing to move their deep group of veterans — pay particular attention to center Brook Lopez and wing Derrick Jones Jr., who are on expiring deals — to get back picks and young players to pair with the backcourt they like of Darius Garland and rookie Keaton Wagler. Specifically, the cross-town Lakers like Lopez and Jones, reports Brian Windhorst and Tim MacMahon at the Hoop Collective Podcast (the players would love that, then they wouldn't have to move). Nothing is imminent. With Brandon Ingram back, the 4-12 Clippers want to see if their fortunes turn, but don't be surprised if they are dealing by the deadline. Other trade rumors • One player "widely expected by league personnel to be dealt by the trade deadline" is Brooklyn's Michael Porter Jr., reports Brian Lewis at the New York Post . The one obstacle to trading Porter? He makes $40.8 million this season. • Denver would like to trade Zeke Nnaji, Fischer reports. Nnaji is under contract for $7.5 million this season with a player option for the same amount next season. • The Utah Jazz might be a team to watch at the deadline, owner Ryan Smith wants to start winning and the Jazz are not so far, Fischer reports.

stories.title: LeBron James has his 1st triple-double for the 76ers in a win over the Heat
stories.summary: — LeBron James had 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds for his first triple-double with Philadelphia, and Tyrese Maxey scored 30 points to lead the 76ers to a 111-104 victory over the Miami Heat in an NBA Cup game Wednesday night.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- — LeBron James had 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds for his first triple-double with Philadelphia, and Tyrese Maxey scored 30 points to lead the 76ers to a 111-104 victory over the Miami Heat in an NBA Cup game Wednesday night. Giannis Antetokounmpo had 32 points and 14 rebounds for Miami, and Davion Mitchell scored 20 points. The 76ers played a second straight game without Joel Embiid (illness), and Jaylen Brown was ruled out after the first half with left hamstring tightness . Brown missed two games last week because of the hamstring injury and hurt it again at the end of the second quarter. Brown, who scored six points, grabbed at his left hamstring, checked himself out the game and walked straight to the locker room. James did it all in their absence. Heat coach Erik Spoelstra coached James when the Heat won consecutive NBA championships in 2012 and 2013. Spoelstra said of James ahead of the game, "Father Time always wins. But right now, he’s giving Father Time hell.” James, who turns 42 on Dec. 30, brought it against Miami when he scored 14 straight points in the first half that gave the 76ers a 47-39 lead and sent the crowd into an absolute frenzy. James' run started simple enough with a three-point play. He buried one long 3, then ripped a longer one from the top of the arc for nine straight. His third 3, that was for show. James hit it from the left side and gave a little shrug. He bobbed his head and licked his lips as the Heat called a timeout and the “LeBron, LeBron, LeBron” remix song played in the arena. He powered down the lane for a layup for 14 straight points. Well shy of the 25 consecutive points he scored in a 2007 playoff game against Detroit. More than enough for the Sixers in a needed rebound victory after they allowed 19-pointers and were blown out by Portland on Monday. James capped his highlight reel with a ridiculous transition alley-oop pass from beyond halfcourt to VJ Edgecombe for a 98-84 lead. He grabbed his 10th rebound with 1:44 left to secure his first triple-double as a Sixer. Up next Heat: At New York on Friday night. 76ers: At Indiana on Friday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

stories.title: NBA Cup 2026: LeBron James nabs triple-double as 76ers snap Heat's 7-game win streak despite losing Jaylen Brown to hamstring injury
stories.summary: James became the oldest player in NBA history to record a triple-double.
stories.detailText: 76ers star LeBron James shot 4 of 6 from 3-point land in a 111-104 win over the Miami Heat on Nov. 25 at Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Mitchell Leff via Getty Images Early in the second quarter Wednesday night in NBA Cup group play, LeBron James pulled up from Broad Street. He drilled a 35-foot 3-pointer amid a torrid stretch that saw him make a trio of triples and score 14 straight points for the 76ers on Thanksgiving Eve. Before that sequence, the Sixers were trailing the Miami Heat by three points at Philadelphia’s Xfinity Mobile Arena. Afterward, they were up eight. While becoming the oldest player in NBA history to notch a triple double — at 41 years and 330 days old — James continued his recent hot streak from beyond the arc, going 4 of 6 on 3-point attempts. Philadelphia, as a team, shot 14 of 35 from long range en route to a 111-104 victory . The Heat (10-7) would have clinched East Group B had they come out on top, but Philadelphia (15-4) denied Miami an eighth consecutive win, despite losing Jaylen Brown to a hamstring injury late in the first half and Joel Embiid being sidelined by illness. Nick Nurse’s squad is now 2-1 in NBA Cup competition, whereas Erik Spoelstra’s Heat dropped to that same mark. James finished with a season-high 25 points and 12 assists, plus 10 rebounds, with maybe his most notable dime taking place in the infancy of the fourth quarter. The 22-time All-Star flexed his elite court vision, timing a halfcourt lob perfectly to connect with VJ Edgecombe for a layup. James later dialed up an alley-oop for forward Dominick Barlow to throw down. Edgecombe was among the Sixers players stepping up in the absence of Brown and Embiid, as Philadelphia protected its nine-point halftime lead and kept Miami at arm’s length over the final two quarters. He had 18 points, and Tyrese Maxey poured in 30. The Heat, who wound up trailing by 16 late in the final frame, were led by Giannis Antetokounmpo, who clocked out with 32 points, 14 rebounds and 4 assists. stories.title: LeBron triple-double, Maxey 30-piece lead Sixers over Heat
stories.summary: Incredible contributions from LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey led the Sixers (sans Joel Embiid) to a relatively-comfortable win over the Heat on Wednesday.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 25: Tyrese Maxey #0 and LeBron James #23 of the Philadelphia 76ers react against the Miami Heat after the second quarter during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup at Xfinity Mobile Arena on November 25, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia 76ers got back in the win column on Wednesday evening, taking down the visiting Miami Heat 111-104 in NBA Cup group play. Joel Embiid was ruled out for this one after having been doubtful on the injury report since yesterday because of illness. This was the second game in a row Embiid missed due to being sick. The Sixers were led by tremendous nights from LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey. James, who notched his first triple-double as a Sixer, put up 25 points on 9-for-15 field goal and 4-for-6 three-point shooting with 12 assists, 10 rebounds and a steal. Maxey added 30 points shooting 12-for-21 from the floor. VJ Edgecombe came alive in the second half to chip in 18 points. The bad news is that Jaylen Brown exited the game just before halftime after seemingly favoring and grabbing at his hamstring. He was quickly ruled out for the rest of the contest with hamstring tightness. Something to be aware of going forward, for sure. The good news is that the Sixers are now 15-4 and have off tomorrow. They’re back in action Friday. Here are some thoughts at the buzzer. First Quarter It didn’t take long to see how Miami benefits from being third in the association in pace. In the first three minutes, the Heat got out ahead in transition three separate times for easy buckets before the Sixers defense even made it back up the other end. The Sixers aren’t that slow, but the Heat were running circles around them early. Jabari Walker got his third start tonight in Joel Embiid’s absence, and it went right to work doing the little things right. He buried a second-chance triple off a LeBron James offensive rebound then got down the defensive end to draw an offensive foul out of Giannis. Jabari had seven points on 3-for-3 field goal shooting in his first six minutes on the floor. If you read any of the Bell Ringers I usually write, you know I cannot stop talking about LeBron’s passing. Well, I’m here to talk about it again. It’s not just one pass. It’s every single pass he makes. He waits until the exact millisecond to release perfectly targeted passes that set up the Sixers for sometimes wide open buckets. LeBron James with your average perfect bounce pass here to a cutting Tyrese Maxey. The usual. pic.twitter.com/YuL83runov — Liberty Ballers (@Liberty_Ballers) November 25, 2026 Tyrese Maxey led the way for the Sixers’ scoring in the first quarter with 13 points on 5-for-8 field goal, 1-for-2 three-point shooting. The consistent contribution of points helped steady the Sixers’ offense after starting off the game a bit disjointed. Philly trailed Miami by three points after one. Second Quarter LeBron has this tendency to just absolutely lock in offensively in insane bursts. He goes from the main facilitator to a mode of “hold on y’all, I got this myself” and, in year 24, he’s absolutely still got it. James had the ball in his hands for three straight Sixers’ possessions and turned each into three points — one and-1, and two threes. He wasn’t done. A minute later, he pulled up again from not far over midcourt for the ultimate heat check. Three more points. It ended up being a 14-3 Sixers run that gave them the lead, courtesy of LeBron James, single-handed. It’s been a very quiet night so far from Jaylen Brown. With just four minutes left in the half, Brown has two points on 1-for-6 field goal shooting with not much else to show for himself on the stat sheet. He hasn’t made a ton of mistakes, necessarily, but more so has been relatively inconsequential so far and can’t seem to get a shot to fall. A far cry from last game, his return from a hamstring strain, where he looked as solid as ever. Just a quick note (and, yes, I admit in saying this I am incredibly biased)… Giannis gets a VERY friendly whistle. I get it, he’s a superstar. But compare the amount of contact he takes that is getting called a foul versus the amount of contact Tyrese Maxey takes with no whistles. The Sixers — especially considering the absence of Joel Embiid — are doing a great job so far containing Bam Adebayo. At halftime, Adebayo had just five points on 2-for-8 field goal shooting The Sixers ended the half on a 7-0 run to help them to a 62-53 lead going into the break. That’s the good news. That bad news is that Brown left the half a few seconds early after seemingly favoring his left leg and grabbing at his hamstring. He went straight back to the locker room. Third Quarter The team was quick to rule out Brown for the rest of the game due to hamstring tightness. Dean Wade started the second half in his spot. Philadelphia has had a tendency to come out of halftime looking a bit sluggish or out of sorts… not tonight. The Sixers ripped off a quick 7-0 run just a minute or so into the second half to push their lead to double-digits. It was the usual suspects, James and Maxey, chipping in with the addition of VJ Edgecombe getting involved. Edgecombe had a relatively quiet first half, but he seemed energized to come out for the second. The sophomore assisted the Sixers’ first two buckets of the third frame and then scored the next two himself. He added a triple and a steal a few minutes later. That’s one thing that Edgecombe seems to possess beyond his years: patience. It doesn’t matter how few opportunities he gets early on in a game, he never gets discouraged and is always ready whenever he is called upon. VJ Edgecombe knocks down the three and he's got 7 points, 2 assists and a steal already in Q3! pic.twitter.com/lPVfoXnKRZ — Liberty Ballers (@Liberty_Ballers) November 25, 2026 It’s a different game entirely when the Sixers are actually hitting their three-pointers. With just a few minutes left in the third, six Sixers have sank at least one three-pointer and three players have multiple. They’re shooting 45.8% from long range and it certainly makes holding on to a narrow lead just a bit easier. It’s been very nice to have Dominick Barlow back. In just his third game of the season after making his debut this past Saturday, Barlow continued putting in some really serviceable minutes at the backup center position featuring solid rim protection, grabbing offensive boards, putting back buckets and setting some big screens. He and Walker have been a decent one-two punch at the center position without Embiid available tonight. Fourth Quarter The Sixers brought a nine-point lead into the final frame. Their lead was quickly extended back into the double-digits with two back-to-back triples from Anfernee Simons — his first two field goals of the night, making him the seventh Sixer to knock down a three-pointer in this one. Apologies for the redundancy but the Lebron passes just get more and more ridiculous. It is just beyond anything I’ve ever seen done so well night in and night out, every single game. Here’s an absurdly accurate lob to Edgecombe from half court to extend the Sixers lead to 14. Ridiculous LeBron James Pass of the Game comes tonight from the King himself, notching his fifth double-double of the season. Absolutely ridiculous. pic.twitter.com/gFdlbmWRVz — Erin Grugan (@eringrugan) November 26, 2026 Edgecombe has absolutely come alive since halftime. From all the statistical contributions to just the extra effort plays that won’t show on the sheet, he has his handprints all over this second half and was a big factor in the Sixers holding on to this lead. The Heat aren’t just going away quietly tonight. They’ve chipped the Sixers lead back down to just single digits with five minutes to play. This Philly team just always has to keep games interesting… What a night from LeBron James! With his 10th rebound with under two minutes to play, James notched his first triple-double as a Philadelphia 76er. The Sixers hold on and get back in the win column. They move to 15-4 on the season and will be back in action on Friday night.

stories.title: LeBron James records first triple-double with 76ers: Where he ranks on all-time list
stories.summary: LeBron James recorded his first triple-double with the 76ers in their game against the Heat.
stories.detailText: In case you forgot, LeBron James is great. The NBA's all-time leading scorer notched his first triple-double with the Philadelphia 76ers Wednesday, Nov. 25 in an NBA Cup matchup against the Miami Heat . He completed the feat with 1:43 left in the fourth quarter, when he scooped his 10th rebound. With Joel Embiid sidelined to start the game and Jaylen Brown getting banged up just seconds before the end of the first half, James took over. He erupted in the second quarter, burying 3-pointer after 3-pointer. During one stretch in the second period, he scored 14 consecutive points for the 76ers . "It's not my job to dominate every night for this ball club," James told reporters after the game. "We have a Finals MVP (Jaylen Brown), a regular season MVP (Joel Embiid), an up-and-coming superstar point guard (Tyrese Maxey), a young fella in VJ (Edgecombe), who is up and coming as well. My dues is paid in what I've done, but if they need me to dust off the cape from time to time, I can still accomplish that. But it's not my job. I don't think it's my job, but if they need it, I can do it." James finished the game with 25 points on 9-of-15 shooting, adding 12 assists and those 10 rebounds. His point and assist totals were both season highs. This is the 126th triple-double in James' career, which has now reached an NBA-record 24 seasons. Russell Westbrook holds the record for most triple-doubles in NBA history with 209. James ranks fifth behind Westbrook, Nikola Jokic, Oscar Robertson and Magic Johnson. No other player in NBA history had recorded a triple-double after turning 41 years old; James has now done it four times. In fact, James now has more triple-doubles than Michael Jordan, Kobe Bryant and Larry Bird — combined. James was ranked the 19th-best player in the league in USA TODAY's preseason rankings of the top 100 players. The four-time MVP and NBA champion joined the 76ers this offseason as a free agent after leaving the Los Angeles Lakers . "We all know, and everybody always says it, but Father Time wins," Heat coach Erik Spoelstra said. "But right now, he's giving Father Time hell." Most triple-doubles in NBA history Through Wednesday, Nov. 25 Russel Westbrook — 209 Nikola Jokic — 202 Oscar Robertson — 181 Magic Johnson — 138 LeBron James — 126 Wilt Chamberlain — 109 Jason Kidd — 107 This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: LeBron James records first triple-double with 76ers: Where he ranks on all-time list

stories.title: The Lakers’ wing depth, adaptability are becoming strengths this season
stories.summary: Los Angeles has gotten valuable contributions from an assortment of forwards to begin the year
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 27: Deni Avdija #8 of the Portland Trail Blazers passes around Matisse Thybulle #4 and Ziaire Williams #11 of the Los Angeles Lakers during a 136-129 Blazers win at Crypto.com Arena on October 27, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Entering 2026-27, perhaps the most consequential unknown resided on the wings for the Los Angeles Lakers. They knew they could count on Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves to provide All-Star-caliber (and better) production in the backcourt. They were banking on Walker Kessler, at worst, providing high-level rim protection and interior play-finishing, based on his tenure with the Utah Jazz. Filling in the gaps at small forward and power forward, as well as minutes off the bench at those spots, was a more dubious proposition. Jake LaRavia was coming off a very poor second half in 2025-26. Matisse Thybulle had battled injuries in recent years while Ziaire Williams was yet to establish firm footing through five NBA seasons. Quentin Grimes’ role and performance had been a little sporadic the past few seasons. Yet five weeks into 2026-27, all of them are donning different caps and playing darn good basketball for the 15-3 Lakers — the product of a team-first, resilient mindset. “I think they’re all really grateful to be here, to be Lakers. They’re all really grateful to be on this team and be part of the group. I know [Matisse] has expressed that to me on a couple of occasions. For [Ziaire], Matisse, [Quentin], they’ve experienced adversity in their careers in different ways,” head coach JJ Redick said after Monday’s win over the Utah Jazz.“ I think that gratitude piece is like…they’re just all in a situation where they’re putting the team first and they’re putting their egos aside. That stuff matters. I think it’s one of the reasons our group has had early success because we said on day one, we wanted this season to be about the team and not any one individual one of us and, so far, it’s been that.” Averaging 2.3 steals and 1.0 blocks per game while shooting 40.5% from deep, Thybulle has been a defensive menace and knocked down open 3s when the ball swings his way. Williams has assumed a lot of lofty point-of-attack duties and excelled as a spot-up shooter (42.1% beyond the arc) and cutter (73.5% on 2-pointers). Grimes scaled up his offensive role while Reaves was sidelined for two weeks and recorded three 20-point outings over that span (including a career-high 47 against the Charlotte Hornets). He’s also shooting 40.3% from deep. LaRavia has rebounded from a bumpy end to last season to shoot 43.2% beyond the arc, relentlessly attack the offensive glass and be a reliable help defender. Dončić, Reaves and Kessler may be leading the way but Los Angeles wouldn’t have charged to the top of the league without their versatile quartet on the wings. “I think just everyone is willing to sacrifice for the same goal. We just have a lot of adaptable players, I think,” Jake LaRavia told reporters postgame on Monday. “A lot of it’s lineup-based, matchup-based, so whoever the coaches think should start that night is who’s going to start. I think, as players, we’re all willing to be kind of thrown in and out of the lineup and it doesn’t really change much for us as players. You just keep the same mindset and keep the same goal and just go out there and play hard.” You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .

Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Noah Graham/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Golden State Warriors are looking to build on Sunday’s momentum, after they snapped a five-game losing streak with a shocking victory over the Boston Celtics . The good news for the Warriors is that they’re facing the 2-15 Sacramento Kings . The bad news for the Warriors is that they’re still not very healthy. Here’s the full injury report for both squads. Warriors Out — Steph Curry (right oblique tear) The Warriors remain optimistic that Curry’s injury won’t linger for too much longer, but there’s still no timeline for a return. Out — Jimmy Butler III (right ACL repair surgery) Out — Moses Moody (left patellar tendon repair surgery) Out — Kristaps Porziņģis (not with team) Same stuff as usual with this trio. Nothing of note! Questionable — Brandon Williams (left hamstring strain) The Warriors have to wait a while longer for Curry, but thankfully may be getting Williams back. Williams had a very honest assessment of how Golden State’s offense has looked without their two-time MVP, and hopefully his lightning bolt scoring off the bench can help fix that. Questionable — Yaxel Lendeborg (illness) Needless to say, the Warriors will be in much worse shape if their star rookie is unable to play toinght. Here’s hoping he’s good to go. Kings Out — Ben Simmons (right Achilles tendon repair surgery) Count me among those who were very curious to see how Simmons would look with the Kings this year. What a bummer to have him suffer a severe injury in training camp. Out — Maxime Raynaud (right patella subluxation) After a very impressive rookie season, Raynaud has yet to make his sophomore debut. Thankfully the second-round pick should be back on the court before too long. Questionable — Zach LaVine (right knee soreness) LaVine can still fill up the points column when he wants to, though he’s openly ceded first option status to rookie Darius Acuff Jr. Even so, the two-time All-Star is averaging 20.3 points per game, and if he’s unable to play tonight, that will be a big hit for Sacramento. Enjoy the game, Dub Nation. It tips off at 7:00 p.m. PT on NBC Sports Bay Area.

stories.summary: Let’s talk turkeys and trap games, Dub Nation. The night before Thanksgiving, the Sacramento Kings roll into Chase Center at 2-15, losers of nine of their last 10, with absolutely nothing to lose. The night before Thanksgiving, the Sacramento Kings roll into Chase Center at 2-15, losers of nine of their last 10, with absolutely nothing to lose. That’s the most dangerous guest you can have at the table. They’re starving for wins! The Warriors (9-8, 11th in the West) have won seven straight at home and come in as the betting favorites, so on paper this is a comfortable Cup Night. Paper doesn’t box out, though. Golden State is 1-4 in the five games Stephen Curry has missed, and that one win came Sunday when they squeezed past Boston 88-87 to snap a five-game skid. Sacramento also beat Boston by one on Saturday, so this is the battle of Pacific Division teams who have recently seen Jayson Tatum bow his head in shame. Brandin Podziemski led the way with 18 points, seven rebounds and four threes. Charles Bassey went 6-for-7 for 13 points with nine rebounds, three assists and three steals, and Gui Santos added 13. Yaxel Lendeborg chipped in 12 points and 8 boards. With Steph Curry, Jimmy Butler, the center post designated for Kristaps Porzingis, and Moses Moody in street clothes, this is the blueprint for now. We’re talking winning ugly, physical, and with everybody eating. The rookie duel between Big Yax (if he plays) and Sacramento’s Darius Acuff Jr. could very well be the best part of the night. Acuff Jr., the No. 7 pick, is averaging 24.6 points and 7.2 assists on a team with two wins. Sacramento asks him to create a whole lot of offense every night for a team going nowhere fast. Lendeborg is putting up 19.2 points a night with 7.4 rebounds, and he’s questionable with an illness. With Steph out and Lendeborg up in the air, Golden State might spend Wednesday trying to figure out how to replace the offense its own rookie creates. Per the latest injury report , here’s the Warriors’ list: Stephen Curry: OUT (right oblique tear; re-evaluation scheduled for Thanksgiving) Jimmy Butler: OUT (right ACL surgery) Moses Moody: OUT (left patellar tendon surgery) Kristaps Porzingis: OUT (not with team) Yaxel Lendeborg: QUESTIONABLE (illness) Brandon Williams: QUESTIONABLE (left hamstring strain) Wednesday will be Steph’s sixth straight game in street clothes.

stories.title: NBA announces $11 billion investment plan to develop, modernize arenas for NBA Europe
stories.summary: A key part of the financial plan for NBA Europe is to modernize — read: Americanize — basketball arenas on the continent.
stories.detailText: Is European basketball ready for modern American-style NBA arenas? With adjacent entertainment districts around them? The NBA announced plans Wednesday for a €10 billion (nearly $11 million at current exchange rates) initiative to pay for "the development and renovation of basketball arenas – and the sports and entertainment districts around them – across Europe." To make this happen, the NBA assembled a group of heavy-hitter global investment firms including Apollo Sports Capital; Ares Management; Arctos, a business of KKR; Blackstone; HPS Investment Partners, a part of BlackRock; J.P. Morgan; Sixth Street and Stonepeak, among others. "We've seen firsthand how state-of-the-art arenas and the related developments around them can transform basketball teams and their surrounding communities," NBA Commissioner Adam Silver said in a statement announcing the initiative. "As we prepare to launch a new league in Europe alongside FIBA, we see a significant opportunity to help clubs develop facilities which both build on the unique traditions that define European basketball while also elevating the fan experience and attracting many more live events." This is about arenas for NBA Europe teams, the league the NBA and partner FIBA plan to at least soft launch next October. That said, this initiative is entirely separate from the team investment process. League officials have been open from the start that they see opportunity in Europe, not just because of the fan base, but because the arena infrastructure there does not maximize profitability — the NBA believes European clubs are leaving money on the table. Part of the plan to make NBA Europe profitable is to change that. In its announcement, the NBA put it this way: "The investors will look to partner with participating clubs, ownership groups, local developers and other service providers to develop world-class arenas that improve the fan experience and, where appropriate, mixed-use districts around them. Depending on local needs and opportunities, these projects could include housing, workplaces, restaurants, retail and public spaces, helping to revitalize communities where people live, work and play. " The NBA has long championed the idea that new world-class arenas drive economic growth in the cities where they are placed, not only through ticket sales and jobs created, but also by revitalizing parts of a city if there are housing and entertainment districts (with restaurants, theaters and more) around them. However, multiple studies suggest this is more a redistribution of wealth and spending from other parts of a city to the new district. Europe does not have many arenas like the ones NBA teams often play in. The target cities for NBA Europe include Paris, Rome, London, Manchester, Lyon, Madrid, Barcelona, Athens, Berlin and more. However, those cities have not been finalized as the bidding process continues.

stories.title: Austin Reaves returns to Lakers practice, might play Friday at San Antonio
stories.summary: The team's second-leading scorer is a full participant Wednesday during practice after missing two weeks because of a bruised left heel.
stories.detailText: Lakers guard Austin Reaves, right, has missed five games since injuring his left heel on Nov. 11. (Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times) After missing two weeks because of a bruised left heel, Lakers guard Austin Reaves returned to live play in practice Wednesday and could be on track to return in time for the Lakers’ early season litmus test against the Spurs at San Antonio on Friday. Lakers coach JJ Redick deadpanned that Reaves’ practice performance Wednesday, the team’s last session before traveling on Thanksgiving Day, was “the best I’ve ever seen him play.” Reaves was more understated. “It felt good to play basketball again,” Reaves said. “Wind was a little bad, but kind of to be expected being out [for] two weeks. But felt good. We’ll see how I wake up tomorrow. We’re still going in the right direction, but felt really good today.” Reaves, the Lakers’ second-leading scorer, missed five games in which the Lakers (15-3) went 4-1 and remained atop the NBA standings to set up Friday’s marquee matchup between the top two teams in the league. He was injured on Nov. 11 during the third quarter against the Milwaukee Bucks when on a dunk attempt, twisting in the air and landing so hard on the inside edge of his heel that he noticed an indent on his shoe insole. He tried to keep playing, but a painful baseline drive forced him to ask out of the game. “I didn’t think I broke my foot,” Reaves said Wednesday, “but it sure felt like I broke my foot.” While managing the pain during his return to play, Reaves has worked with the training staff to find a comfortable sneaker and insole combination. Reaves said through the seemingly million options presented to him, he found one that worked for Wednesday’s practice. Read more: Lakers eagerly await Austin Reaves' return before epic showdown against San Antonio “He looked really good today,” center Walker Kessler said. “It was definitely good to have him back out there.” After signing a maximum contract extension to establish himself as one of the Lakers’ top stars, Reaves got off to a strong start to the season. He is averaging 24.7 points, 4.7 assists and 3.3 rebounds while shooting a career-best 51.3% from the field and 40.9% from three. The Lakers had won six consectutive games heading into the Milwaukee matchup when Reaves got hurt. Even when Reaves was sidelined, they stretched the streak to nine, tying the longest in Redick’s coaching tenure. “I was just frustrated because it’s one of those things, it’s like an uncontrollable,” Reaves said. “... One of those things that just, it sucks. I was rolling, playing well. We were rolling as a team, wanted to continue to be out there and play games. Hate missing games. But it’s one of those things, like I said, there wasn’t much that we could really do, but we took care of business.” The Lakers’ offense has stalled without Reaves, dropping from first in scoring and efficiency to third. Luka Doncic is especially struggling with his shot. The league’s leading scorer, averaging 36.6 points per game, has made 12 of 51 (23.5%) shots from three during the last four games. With Reaves out, Doncic got help from reserve guards Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton. Grimes started in Reaves’ place and delivered a game-saving, career-high 47 points against the Charlotte Hornets. Sexton served as a primary ballhandler during critical fourth-quarter stretches without Doncic. “[We] found ways to win,” Reaves said. “I think that’s a big part of the NBA is if you can find ways to win when you’re not playing as good as you are capable of, that’ll help win in a lot of games. So very happy, proud just to continue to see the togetherness and the growth that we continue to have.” The Lakers stuck together to set up Friday’s showdown that is stocked with intriguing storylines. The NBA Cup group stage finale is a win-and-you’re-in matchup for the knockout round. Most valuable player candidates Doncic and Victor Wembanyama, averaging 29.9 points, 12.3 rebounds and 3.9 blocks a game, face off for the first time this season. Questioned for a perceived weaker schedule, the Lakers get their first major opportunity to assert themselves into the title conversation against the reigning Western Conference champions. The Spurs (15-3) have the best net rating in the NBA, outscoring opponents by 12.3 points per 100 possessions. The Lakers, suddenly a top-10 defensive team after holding the Utah Jazz to only 94 points in Monday’s win, are sixth in net rating (plus-6.8 points per 100 possessions). Despite all the makings of an epic early-season showdown, Redick emphasized that Friday’s blockbuster matchup is only the beginning of a difficult four-game road trip. After San Antonio, the Lakers play at Memphis on Sunday, Houston on Monday and New Orleans on Wednesday. “I think these four games will be a great barometer of where we’re at,” Redick said. “To your point whether it’s guys being in and out of the lineup or play-style changes or tweaks we make or rotation changes, it just always evolves. “And whether we lose the game, whether we win the game, we’re either going to be contenders on ‘First Take’ or we’re not going to be contenders and we’re fake. That stuff is just noise. We’re going to focus on the process of trying to get better and it’s a good test to see where we’re at.” Sign up for our weekly newsletter on all things Lakers. This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

stories.title: Lakers’ red-hot start to season will strike fear in Celtics fans hearts
stories.summary: Historically, the Lakers' hot start to the season suggests an NBA title is on the way.
stories.detailText: The Lakers are on a quest to become a championship-level team . And if history can be an indicator, their hot start to the 2026-27 NBA season suggests they’re on the right path. Lakers star guards Luka Doncic (77) and Austin Reaves (15). NBAE via Getty Images With Monday’s home win over the Jazz , the Lakers improved to 15-3 on the season, which was not only tied with the Spurs for the league’s best record, but also a positive sign for the Lakers’ hopes of being title contenders. This season is the sixth time this century the Lakers have started a season by winning at least 15 of their first 18 games. All five of those seasons ended with the Lakers making the NBA Finals, including winning the title in four of them. Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick watches his players. AP Photo/Kyusung Gong The other five times since 2000 that the Lakers won at least 83 percent of their first 18 games were: 2001-2002 (16-2), 2003-04 (15-3), 2008-09 (16-2), 2009-10 (15-3) and 2019-20 (16-2). They won the 2002, ‘09, ‘10 and ‘20 championships after their hot start to those seasons. They made it to the Finals in 2004, which was their fourth championship series appearance in five years, before losing to the Pistons in five games. Walker Kessler, left, and Luka Doncic high-five during a game. NBAE via Getty Images The Lakers have won at least 15 of their first 18 games 13 times in franchise history. Half (six of 13) of those seasons ended with them winning the NBA title, while three more ended with them at least making it to the NBA Finals. Another commonality between those seasons is that the Lakers won at least 54 regular season games (or the equivalent of it in an 82-game season in the case of the pandemic-shortened 2019-20) each time they had such a hot start to the season. For a team that was projected to be a borderline playoff contender, that’s great company to be in — a high standard to live up to — but also a sign they’re on the right path.

stories.title: RJ Luis suing SEC and Greg Sankey after LSU basketball eligibility fight
stories.summary: Former LSU men's basketball player RJ Luis has filed a lawsuit against the SEC and commissioner Greg Sankey seeking damages after his eligibility battle
stories.detailText: The saga that's engulfed LSU , the Tigers ' men's basketball program and the SEC has taken yet another turn. And, to the surprise of no one, it involves lawyers. RJ Luis, the one-time LSU men's basketball player whose eligibility case has been a point of contention for weeks with the SEC, has filed a lawsuit against the SEC and commissioner Greg Sankey seeking damages caused by the conference's efforts that prompted LSU's decision not to play him following a previously awarded court injunction, acccording to a motion and other documents provided by one of Luis' attorneys to The Daily Advertiser , a part of the USA TODAY Network. REQUIRED READING: LSU played chicken with the SEC — and finally blinked. Was it worth it? | Opinion It's unclear how much Luis is seeking in damages. Luis, who had previously signed NBA contracts with the Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics, was granted two separate injunctions in Louisiana courts, the first on Aug. 3 and another Nov. 13, as he sought eligibility for the 2026-27 college basketball season. Luis committed to play for Tigers coach Will Wade in May. While Luis was cleared to play by the judicial system, he faced an additional obstacle with the SEC, which in August passed a rule barring member institutions from having athletes compete for them who had previously declared for the NFL, NBA or WNBA drafts. Following the Nov. 13 injunction, the SEC issued a statement saying it would abide by the court's order and not punish LSU for putting Luis on its roster, but the league mentioned nothing about the Tigers actually playing Luis. On Nov. 18, however, Luis played 15 minutes, scoring 11 points and pulling down nine rebounds, in his team's 79-67 victory against Louisiana Monroe. One day later, LSU president Wade Rousseau released a statement saying he instructed Wade not to play Luis , who has since been removed from the LSU roster and hasn't played in the team's two most recent games. That didn't mark the end of the escalating tensions between LSU and the league of which it's a founding member. The SEC's chancellors and presidents are scheduled to hold a vote on Dec. 3 over whether to expel the Tigers from the conference. A two-thirds vote from the 15 non-LSU members is required for the action to pass. A 6-foot-7 guard/forward, Luis averaged 18.2 points and 7.2 rebounds per game for St. John's during the 2024-25 season, which culminated with him being named Big East player of the year and earning All-American honors. He declared for the 2025 NBA Draft, but was not selected by a team. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: RJ Luis suing SEC and Greg Sankey after LSU basketball eligibility fight

NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Kenny Giarla/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images During the Washington Wizards’ much-needed three-game win streak, they made a few key adjustments. They yanked underperformers out of the rotation and limited the Deandre Ayton solo-big minutes, in which the Wizards have gotten caved in all season. They played Trae Young off the ball more and gave Kyshawn George and AJ Dybantsa more creation responsibility. More than anything, though, they cleaned up some of the low-hanging fruit. They grabbed more rebounds, matched up better in transition, and eased some of the most damaging defensive mistakes. They knocked down some more open threes. The Celtics, in Tuesday night’s primetime (first half) onslaught, showed the Wizards how far they still have to go. Boston is a team built to punish glaring weaknesses. They relentlessly attack bad defenders, and of course were merciless in dragging Young into every action and forcing the Wizards to make difficult rotations. The Celtics scored 80 first half points and poured in 15 threes — the sort of Mazulla-ball explosion that they’ve been waiting to unleash. Too often, the Wizards were slow to react to the Celtics’ core actions. Boston, when they’re locked in, is adept at running early-clock plays that prey on inattentive defenses, like this flare screen: In semi-transition, the Wizards are cross-matched, a common hazard of the double-big alignment. The Celtics are on the same page: Neemias Queta steps into a screen for a trailing Jayson Tatum on an unsuspecting Dybantsa. Dybantsa realizes slightly too late that he needs to switch the screen and take Queta. By then, it’s too late. The floor is open, and Queta has cleverly slipped to the basket. (Note, too, that Sarr and Davis are the weak side defenders here. In a few situations on Tuesday night, the Celtics generated open threes by capitalizing on that particular alignment. Sarr and Davis are slower at completing the “X-out” rotation, with the low man swarming the rim and the other playing two shooters at once.) Here’s another classic Celtics action, which Kevin analyzed in his recap : Again, the Celtics get right into their action. Derrick White is set up for a Spain, or stack, pick-and-roll — where he sets a back-screen on a dropping big man. White is still so valuable to the Celtics, despite his ice-cold shooting, in part because of plays like this; he is clever about screening his own man and disguising his intentions. On this one, White’s screen slams Ayton and springs Paul George into the paint. The problem there starts with Dybantsa, who is hit hard by Luka Garza’s initial screen and forced into a switch. To his credit, Tre Johnson sees what’s happening and recovers toward George. But Bilal Coulibaly senses disaster and sprints over to help, leaving Payton Pritchard alone. It’s these emergency defense instincts that the Wizards struggle with. Coulibaly is right that he may be needed at the rim, but he commits so fully that he has no chance to rotate back to Pritchard. The most in-sync defenses are on a string when the offense gains an advantage — perhaps, in this situation, with the guy in Dybantsa’s spot peeling off to the corner. The Wizards have recently been better at erring on the side of effort defensively, and that’s the first step toward building something real. Dybantsa has room to grow on the little things, like screen navigation, but he flies around and pressures relentlessly. Coulibaly knows he’s on the court for his defense and plays like it. When opposing teams line up transition layups and grab endless offensive rebounds, that’s when the pressure on coach Brian Keefe starts heating up. But lately, that pressure is getting a bit lighter, and the second half against the Celtics was much better, with Boston cooling off and the Wizards limiting some of the easiest baskets. They’ll have a few days to rest and take stock before a rematch with the Orlando Magic on Saturday.

stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid will miss Wednesday night's game against the Miami Heat with an illness. After a slow start, Embiid had found his rhythm in recent games, leading the Sixers in scoring (29.7 points per game) in their past three wins. Embiid began the dominant period with a season-high 37 points last Monday against the Brooklyn Nets . The 2023 league MVP said afterward he had realized after reviewing this season's game tape that he hadn't been playing aggressively. Without Embiid, the Sixers will lean on Dominick Barlow , Jabari Walker , and Adem Bona .

stories.title: Lakers star divulges ‘uncomfortable’ reason for success without Austin Reaves
stories.summary: The Lakers had to alter the formula for success.
stories.detailText: For the first four weeks of the season, the Lakers, for the most part, won their games in similar fashion. A scorching start from Luka Doncic en route to a 30-point (and oftentimes, 40-point) performance. Austin Reaves, Doncic’s backcourt co-star, efficiently filled in the gaps offensively en route to an uber-efficient 25-point game. Walker Kessler provided the rim pressure the team needed, which in combination with the scoring/playmaking from Doncic and Reaves, opened up scoring opportunities for the players around them. Luka Doncic #77 and Austin Reaves #15 of the Los Angeles Lakers look on. NBAE via Getty Images Los Angeles Lakers forward Jarred Vanderbilt playing defense. AP Photo/Kyusung Gong The recipe not only led to the Lakers winning 12 of their first 14 games, but also powered them to have the league’s top-ranked offense. But then the formula that led them to most of their early-season victories changed before their longest stretch of games at home. The ingredients changing meant the recipe for success also had to be altered – which the Lakers successfully pulled off during the 3–1 homestand that ended with Monday’s victory over the Jazz . Doncic cooled off from his sizzling start to the season during the homestand, averaging 29.5 points (38.5% shooting, 23.5% on 3-pointers), after averaging 39 points (48.6% shooting, 40.6% on 3s) beforehand. Utah Jazz forward Kyle Filipowski (2) goes up for a basket as Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler (14) defends. AP Photo/Kyusung Gong Reaves wasn’t available, missing the last five games because of a bruised left heel. The Lakers are hopeful he’ll return during Friday’s road game against the Spurs. Which led to the Lakers leaning on their defense to pull out most of their recent wins. “We have a standard and we have to play to that standard and do what we’re supposed to,” Collin Sexton said. “When you’re playing to a standard, it doesn’t matter who’s in and who’s out. We all have to help. It doesn’t matter who’s coming into the game, we all have a role to play to do what the person in front of us did.” The Lakers held the Hornets to 114 points in their overtime win Nov. 17, allowed 109 points in the Nov. 18 loss to the Jazz , held the Kings to 104 points in Friday’s win before holding the Jazz to 94 points on Monday, which is the fewest amount of points a team has scored against the Lakers this season. Los Angeles Lakers forward Jarred Vanderbilt (2) vies for the ball against Utah Jazz forward Kyle Filipowski. AP Photo/Kyusung Gong Their halfcourt defense has been a strength of the Lakers throughout the season. But they cleaned up some of their transition defensive concerns. They remained disruptive, recording at least 16 turnovers in each game of the homestand. And using more zone defense, sometimes with full-court pressure, gave the Lakers a boost on that end of the floor. “We have a lot of like disruptors defensively,” Jake LaRavia said. “We do a good job at just creating pressure for the other team, whether it’s deflections or just ball pressure, and kind of making them uncomfortable in bringing the ball up the court. It’s obviously been working for us, so we’re going to keep doing it ’til it stops working.” The Lakers’ defensive rating improved from No. 17 to No. 10 during the homestand – albeit against inferior opponents that have a combined record of 9–43. They’re going to need Reaves available and improved play from Doncic as the level of competition picks up with the four-game trip post-Thanksgiving that features matchups against the Spurs, Grizzlies and Rockets. Those are three of the four teams closest to the Lakers in the top of the Western Conference standings. But even though it wasn’t always pretty, the Lakers showed they can at least win in other ways outside of what they showed in the first few weeks of the season. “Austin is a very, very important piece to this team, and so seeing how we compete without him, not at our full strength, that’s good,” Kessler said. “It builds resiliency. Because [you’re] not going to be always [at] your full strength. Things happen, it’s a long season, so it’s encouraging to see.”

stories.title: NBA plans to invest 10bn euros in European arenas
stories.summary: The NBA steps up its plans for a European league by announcing a strategy to invest at least 10bn euros in the development of basketball arenas across the continent.
stories.detailText: The Intuit Dome, which opened in August 2024 and is home of the LA Clippers, is the newest arena in the NBA [Getty Images] The NBA has stepped up its plans for a European league by announcing a strategy to invest at least 10bn euros in the development and renovation of basketball arenas across the continent. The league has assembled a group of investment firms for the project, which would also look to improve the sports and entertainment districts around the arenas. The initiative forms part of the NBA and the International Basketball Federation's (Fiba) plan to launch a new, professional basketball system in Europe in 2027. It will provide prospective clubs and ownership groups with access to capital and the NBA's expertise in regard to developing modern arenas and their surroundings. "We've seen first-hand how state-of-the-art arenas and the related developments around them can transform basketball teams and their surrounding communities," said NBA commissioner Adam Silver. "As we prepare to launch a new league in Europe alongside Fiba, we see a significant opportunity to help clubs develop facilities which both build on the unique traditions that define European basketball while also elevating the fan experience and attracting many more live events." The NBA's announcement stated that the plans for the areas surrounding arenas could include housing, workplaces, restaurants, retail and public spaces, ensuring they would be year-round destinations. In the statement, the investors said: "We're excited to work with the NBA to support a transformative phase of infrastructure development across Europe. "Together, we have the potential to invest billions of euros to create world-class venues in European cities, honouring the passion and traditions of European basketball fans and supporting lasting economic growth in the communities where the game means so much." The announcement cited a study by The Sports Consultancy, which claimed the NBA and Fiba's league could contribute more than 24bn euros in gross value added to GDP across Europe. It also claimed the league could support nearly 15,000 full-time equivalent jobs annually and attract nearly 70 million spectators over its first 10 years. This summer, the league unveiled the full group stage schedule for this year's in-season tournament, with action taking place every Friday from Oct. 30 to Nov. 27 and on special Cup nights during Thanksgiving week (Nov. 24-25). After the New York Knicks became the first team to win the NBA Cup and Finals in the same season, can Jalen Brunson & Co. keep their championship run going? Tyrese Maxey and LeBron James led the Philadelphia 76ers to a home victory over the Heat on Wednesday to deal Miami its first loss in Cup play and claim the top spot in East Group B. Maxey led Philadelphia with a team-high 30 points, and James posted 25 points, 10 rebounds and 12 assists to register his first triple-double since signing with the 76ers during the offseason. know What is the format? NBA commissioner Adam Silver has had a longstanding fascination with European soccer. Establishing an in-season cup competition within the NBA schedule came from soccer leagues having both a regular-season title, won by the team with the most points over the full year, and a separate tournament (or, in some leagues, multiple tournaments) that runs concurrently with the league season. In England, for example, there are the various divisions -- led by the Premier League -- and also the FA Cup competition. But unlike those European leagues, which play their cup competitions outside of their league schedules, the NBA Cup is built in to the regular-season slate. The 30 NBA teams are split into six five-team groups -- three featuring Eastern Conference teams and three comprising Western Conference teams -- with each team then playing one game against the other four in its group. The winner of each group, plus the team with the best record among the non-group winners, advances to the knockout stage of the competition. How will this impact the regular-season schedule and standings? Typically, the NBA sends out a full 82-game schedule in mid-August. Now, the league sends out only 80 games and leaves a gap of roughly a week to fill in later, depending on how the group stage of the NBA Cup plays out. The two teams from the East and West that lose in the quarterfinals will play their 82nd game against each other. Meanwhile, the 22 teams that fail to qualify for the knockout rounds will have their final two games scheduled -- one at home and one on the road against others eliminated in the group stage. The teams that reach the NBA Cup final will actually play 83 games -- though the championship game won't count toward the standings or any statistical markers. The four teams that reach the semifinals will have completed their 82 games and won't need any other games added to their schedule. Any team that makes it to the semifinals will have that game moved later in the schedule to avoid back-to-back games. The NBA made this change in an effort to avoid having empty days on the calendar while attempting to minimize back-to-backs for all teams as much as possible. Where are the semifinals and final being played? In a shift from previous tournaments, the quarterfinals and semifinals will be played at home sites. The Dec. 11 title game, meanwhile, will move from Las Vegas to the storied Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis. NBA commissioner Adam Silver previously said the league was searching for "storied college arenas" to play host to the Cup final. (No venue has been announced for 2027.) Why does the NBA Cup include regular-season games? Before its launch, one of the main questions surrounding the in-season tournament was why any team would be incentivized to compete in it. The NBA ensured teams will be motivated by making every game part of the season and, as in-conference matchups, potentially important to playoff tiebreakers. If this had been set up like the cup tournaments in European soccer, there would have been nothing stopping NBA teams from opting out by sitting their top players for extra rest. Which teams make up the groups? To create the groups, the NBA put the 15 teams in each conference into five pots, separated by their finish last season. Pot 1 included the teams that finished in the top three in the regular-season standings, Nos. 4-6 in the standings went into Pot 2, Nos. 7-9 into Pot 3, Nos. 10-12 into Pot 4 and Nos. 13-15 into Pot 5. As a result, the following groups were drawn: East Group A Detroit Pistons Toronto Raptors Orlando Magic Milwaukee Bucks Brooklyn Nets East Group B New York Knicks Cleveland Cavaliers Philadelphia 76ers Miami Heat Indiana Pacers East Group C Boston Celtics Atlanta Hawks Charlotte Hornets Chicago Bulls Washington Wizards West Group A Denver Nuggets Houston Rockets Phoenix Suns Dallas Mavericks Utah Jazz West Group B Oklahoma City Thunder Minnesota Timberwolves LA Clippers New Orleans Pelicans Memphis Grizzlies West Group C San Antonio Spurs Los Angeles Lakers Portland Trail Blazers Golden State Warriors Sacramento Kings Does one group stand out the most from the others? East Group B is a monster. All five teams -- defending NBA Cup and Finals champion New York, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Miami and Indiana -- are among the favorites to win the conference in 2026-27. The group stage will also feature reunion games for LeBron James , when the 76ers face the Cavs and Heat. And after guard Tyrese Haliburton missed the entire 2025-26 season while rehabbing a torn Achilles, the Pacers will be back among the East elite and hungry to reach the title game in Indianapolis. What do players get for winning? In 2023, the first year the tournament was held, the players on the winning team received $500,000 each and the runners-up got $200,000. The losing players of the semifinals each got $100,000, and those ousted in the quarterfinals got $50,000. Now, in each subsequent year, the prizes will be slightly higher, as a result of negotiated raises year over year to keep pace with increases in the salary cap and basketball-related income as part of the most recent collective bargaining agreement between the NBA and the National Basketball Players Association. Will anyone earn individual honors for their play in NBA Cup games? There will be an MVP award, as well as an all-tournament team. Will this have any impact on the playoffs? Not beyond the games counting in the regular-season standings (and toward tiebreakers). The only playoff impact comes from the wins and losses accrued throughout the tournament. Though there was debate among league insiders about guaranteeing a playoff berth for winning the tournament, ultimately that idea (or any other to further incentivize teams) was not enacted. Why is it called the Emirates NBA Cup? The league struck a sponsorship deal with Emirates, the Dubai-based airline, to sponsor the tournament after its initial run. The NBA said last year that it went with the most basic titles for both the tournament and its trophy -- the "in-season tournament" and "NBA Cup" -- as a way to introduce the concept to fans. However, using such nondescript names had another clear advantage: It gave the league a blank slate in case it sold the naming rights for the tournament and cup to a sponsor and avoided the complications that could arise by naming them after someone (for example, late NBA commissioner David Stern, one possibility that had been floated before the tournament was officially unveiled). teamStories.detailText: Austin Reaves, who has missed the last five games because of a bruised left heel, was a full participant in Lakers practice on Wednesday but his status remains unknown for Friday’s game against the Spurs. “It felt good to play basketball again,” Reaves said in his first public comments since suffering the injury Nov. 11 . “Wind was a little bad, but kind of to be expected being out two weeks. But felt good. You know, we’ll see how I wake up [Thursday]. We’re still going in the right direction, but felt really good today.” Austin Reaves, left, and Luka Doncic talk during a game against the Utah Jazz in Los Angeles, Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images Reaves sustained the injury after landing awkwardly following a missed fast-break dunk in the third quarter of a game against the Bucks. He said he’s not quite sure what happened on the play. “No, I had no idea,” he said. “Tried to play through it, and then I drove baseline, planted on it, and was like, I can’t do this. So walked to the back and was in some pretty bad pain. I didn’t think I broke my foot, but it sure felt like I broke my foot.” Lakers coach JJ Redick, who suffered a similar injury in April 2016, has repeatedly described the heel bruise as a “pain tolerance issue.” Reaves echoed that Wednesday. “It’s not a strain in your hamstring or something like that,” Reaves said. “It’s kind of just something that’s going to linger around if you continue to play before you’re ready. And basically, the main message was, let’s get this back to normal before we put you back out there and put yourself at risk again so later on in the season you won’t have to deal with a flare up or something.” The Lakers went 4-1 after Reaves suffered the injury, but they clearly missed his offensive production after falling to the Jazz on Nov. 18 , 109-97, and barely squeaking past the Hornets (118-114) and Kings (106-104). Reaves is averaging 24.7 points (51.3% shooting from the field, 40.9% from beyond the arc), 3.3 rebounds and 4.7 assists. “One of those things that just, it sucks,” Reaves said. “You know, I was rolling, playing well. We were rolling as a team, wanted to continue to be out there and play games. Hate missing games. But it’s one of those things, like I said, there wasn’t much that we could really do. But we took care of business.” Austin Reaves #15 of the Los Angeles Lakers reacts during a game against the Utah Jazz at Crypto.com Arena on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images When asked how Reaves looked Wednesday, Redick didn’t hesitate. “Best I’ve ever seen him play,” he said. When reporters prodded him to see if he was being sarcastic, he doubled down, “Yeah, not joking,” he added. Austin Reaves (15) of the Los Angeles Lakers smiles during a game against the Utah Jazz at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images The Lakers sure hope that Reaves can return Friday and that Redick is right considering the challenge they have ahead of them. The Lakers and Spurs are tied for the best record in the NBA at 15-3 and Luka Doncic and Victor Wembanyama are currently in a two-man race for the MVP Award . When asked if it’s important to him to return against the Spurs, Reaves balked. “I mean, I want to play,” Reaves said. “…I didn’t get hurt the night of Milwaukee and look at the schedule and be like, ‘God, I need to be back before the San Antonio game.’ If I’m back, good, we’ll go to war. But I got to listen to my body and take care of myself. But it should be fun if I’m healthy and get out there.”

teamStories.detailText: EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- Los Angeles Lakers guard Austin Reaves returned to his first full practice Wednesday since suffering a left heel bruise two weeks ago, although his status for Friday's game against the San Antonio Spurs is still undetermined. "It's the best I've ever seen him play," said Lakers coach JJ Redick, who insisted he was not joking with his assessment. "He looked good." Reaves, who has missed the Lakers' past five games while rehabbing the injury, added: "It felt good to play basketball again. We'll see how I wake up tomorrow. We're still going in the right direction, but felt really good today." Reaves spoke to reporters about the injury for the first time since he suffered it Nov. 11 against the Milwaukee Bucks , when he landed awkwardly on his left foot after missing a contested dunk in transition. "I think it was just the impact and kind of the way I landed," he said. "I think I was kind of like twisting in the air as well as I came down on the inside [of the heel]." The sixth-year guard was averaging 24.7 points on 51.3% shooting from the floor and 40.9% from 3 with 4.7 assists before the injury. He said he was worried he suffered a major injury at first. "I didn't think I broke my foot, but it sure felt like I broke my foot," he said. "But it was just not much you can really do. Try to stay off of it as much as possible. ... There's not really a certain thing you can do to make the process speed up, you kind of just got to let time take care of those things." He has settled on a pair of sneakers and a supportive insole to wear to help alleviate any lingering pain as he makes his comeback after trying out "a million shoes" and "a million different insoles." The Lakers will fly to San Antonio on Thursday afternoon after members of the team spend time with their families Thanksgiving morning. L.A. and San Antonio are tied atop the Western Conference standings at 15-3. Friday's meeting is also the last NBA Cup qualifier for both teams. San Antonio leads the West's Group C with a 2-0 record; the Lakers are 2-1. San Antonio plays the Portland Trail Blazers in their third NBA Cup qualifier on Wednesday night. No matter what happens in the Spurs-Blazers game, the Lakers can advance to the NBA Cup quarterfinals with a win Friday. Reaves said he has motivation to return for the matchup, but will not compromise his recovery to do so if he is not ready. "I didn't get hurt the night of Milwaukee and look at the schedule and be like, 'God, I need to be back before the San Antonio game,'" Reaves said. "If I'm back, good, we'll go to war. But I got to listen to my body and take care of myself. But it should be fun if I'm healthy and get out there." L.A. has gone 4-1 without Reaves during this recent stretch, and 5-1 overall without him this season. While Redick acknowledged the Lakers' four-game road trip that begins in San Antonio and continues against the Memphis Grizzlies , Houston Rockets and New Orleans Pelicans will be "a challenge," he bucked against drawing any conclusions on L.A.'s overall chances this season based on how the team performs coming up. "We're either going to be contenders or we're going to be a fake team," Redick said of the commentary that would follow the Lakers, no matter what happens on the road trip. "If we win that [San Antonio] game and then we lose to Memphis and Houston, we're back to being a fake team. So ... the overreactions game-to-game are what they are, and we've got to, as a group, manage that and manage the noise and that's just part of being in the NBA."
