stories.title: Sources: Mike McCarthy has Steelers' full support after Aaron Rodgers interview
stories.summary: Mike McCarthy has the full support of the Steelers organization and will remain the team's coach after Aaron Rodgers' allegations, sources told NFL Network and ESPN.
stories.detailText: PITTSBURGH -- Mike McCarthy has the full support of the Pittsburgh Steelers organization and will remain the team's coach after Aaron Rodgers ' stunning allegations Wednesday, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. Sources told Rapoport and Fowler that the Steelers are standing by McCarthy in the wake of Rodgers' bombshell interview on "The Pat McAfee Show" in which the star quarterback accused the longtime coach of sleeping through team meetings. Multiple sources around the NFL corroborated Rodgers' account of McCarthy to ESPN reporters, with one saying: "It's all true." "Obviously we talk regularly, so they're very in tune with everything that goes on in football operations as far as my job responsibility," McCarthy said of ownership and front office involvement in the decision to bench and then release the four-time MVP. "And I think they do a very good job of communicating back and forth. And so it was clearly my decision, and they have supported me 100%." Nearly two hours after Rodgers' interview with McAfee, McCarthy also addressed the sleeping accusation and acknowledged that he did indeed break down the halftime huddle in Philadelphia with, "1, 2, 3 Packers," as the quarterback described. "Well, I think just like anything, the Philadelphia situation, halftime was very emotional, and there's conversations prior to that," McCarthy, a former Packers coach, said. "Embarrassing moment, but I just think we worked a lot of hours, so definitely a difference of opinion from what I was told about the comments." The Steelers announced late Tuesday that they had benched Rodgers in favor of Mason Rudolph and he would be inactive for their Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos . Rodgers told McAfee that he learned of his benching through teammate Pat Freiermuth , and he last spoke with McCarthy around 6:15 p.m. Tuesday. But McCarthy said there were attempts by the Steelers to contact the quarterback throughout the night. "We were going through game-plan meetings, but I know there was continuous efforts to reach Aaron, and I know there was communication with his agents," McCarthy said. He added of the timing: "It got to a point where we felt it was important for Mason to know what was in front of him." McCarthy confirmed it was his decision to bench Rodgers, and the coach said he came to that conclusion after the quarterback issued an ultimatum "made clearly outside of his job description." Sources told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo and Rapoport that Rodgers approached McCarthy about the quarterback taking over playcalling, but McCarthy turned down the idea. One possible compromise was for quarterbacks coach Tom Arth to relay playcalls to Rodgers during the entire game. Arth already relayed plays during the two-minute offense. "I left it with him that if you try and bench me or don't change the playcaller, then you should just release me, because I feel like at this point I'm doing what's right for the organization," Rodgers told McAfee. McCarthy also denied Rodgers' assertion that McCarthy was still holding on to a grudge that stemmed from Rodgers' involvement in McCarthy's 2018 firing from the Green Bay Packers . McCarthy said he would not discuss any personal conversations he had with Rodgers but declared that he thinks he is the right person to lead the Steelers. "I know how to win, and that's the facts," McCarthy said. "This is my third program and I plan on winning here because of the men, because of this organization, what we've got started and the opportunity we have to learn and grow today because of some of the things that frankly should have been talked about earlier. This is a growth opportunity that I intend to take full advantage of." And though Rodgers suggested that McCarthy lost the locker room with his actions, McCarthy said he still believed his players have faith in his ability to lead and coach the team. "Yes, I do," McCarthy said. "And I will say that I just came from a player council meeting. I thought that it was a meeting, very direct, very honest. I appreciated the opportunity to talk through numerous things that have been on their mind, comments that brought discussion to the forefront. So I'm proud of our leadership, I'll say that. And more importantly, I love the urgency that everybody had coming out of that meeting." McCarthy was hired by Pittsburgh in January in large part because of Rodgers' suggestion to interview him for the head coaching vacancy during the quarterback's exit interview with general manager Omar Khan. Rodgers and McCarthy were effusive in their praise of each other early in their reunion, focusing on the heights reached during their 13-year partnership in Green Bay. But that relationship rapidly deteriorated as Rodgers struggled during the Steelers' two-game losing streak, and as Rodgers sought more control of the offense. "I just think like anything, there's a long history there," McCarthy said of his estrangement with Rodgers. "So clearly difference of opinion. I felt like he was given an incredible opportunity. I mean, there's so many great things about what he's done in his career, and this is where we are."

stories.title: What's next for Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy, Steelers?
stories.summary: The news out of Pittsburgh shook the NFL landscape, and ESPN's insiders share insights on the QB, the coach and their futures.
stories.detailText: The Pittsburgh Steelers went from a 6-4 team vying for playoff contention with a four-time MVP quarterback under center Tuesday to a team entering its Week 12 game Friday against the Denver Broncos reeling from controversy and now without Aaron Rodgers on its roster. Pittsburgh waived Rodgers after the quarterback said Wednesday on "The Pat McAfee Show" that he wouldn't return to the team after his stunning benching Tuesday night . It was a scorched-earth interview that included allegations that coach Mike McCarthy has been sleeping through team meetings , among other embarrassing details. Rodgers said he found out from teammate Pat Freiermuth that he was being benched and still hasn't heard the news from McCarthy. The veteran quarterback and the coach's partnership goes back to when they were together in Green Bay as the Packers won Super Bowl XLV and extended to McCarthy being fired eight years later in 2018. Turning 43 on Sunday, Rodgers had known limitations entering the 2026 season. Though his completion percentage (65.7%) in his first season in Pittsburgh was his highest since 2021 (with the Packers), his 3.7 air yards per completion were the lowest in the NFL. Rodgers' 3.9 air yards per completion this season were the third lowest in the past 20 years. The Steelers had a 19.7% chance of winning the AFC North entering Week 10. But after back-to-back losses, they're down to roughly 5%. If Pittsburgh beats Denver, the Steelers' chances of making it to the playoffs will grow to 92%, but a loss reduces those odds to 82%, per ESPN Analytics . Could Rodgers finish out his 22nd season in the league with another team? What does this move mean for the Steelers' offense moving forward? As the story out of Pittsburgh and from Rodgers continues to evolve, ESPN's NFL insiders tackle the most pressing questions on everything they know as of Wednesday afternoon. What were some of the signs that happened in Pittsburgh for this divorce to escalate so quickly? This past year has been a whirlwind of change for the Steelers organization. McCarthy, a then 62-year-old Pittsburgh native, was hired in January to become just the Steelers' fourth head coach since 1969. The news of McCarthy's hire came 11 days after Mike Tomlin told the team he was walking away from the role after 19 seasons. Rodgers even "vouched" for McCarthy to general manager Omar Khan. And then the Steelers brought Rodgers back because the organization believed the four-time MVP was their best option to contend in the AFC, and they inked him to a one-year deal worth up to $25 million after another prolonged offseason courtship. Rodgers previously told reporters that he will retire after this season . Flash forward to this year's training camp and that's when the problems started, Rodgers alleged Wednesday to ESPN's Pat McAfee. Rodgers said it's a "delicate situation because the coaching staff is worried about their job security and the players are worried about their money and their job security. And I don't. I've made money. "And again, I'll reiterate, originally I'm talking about in training camp when this stuff was going on, when he was missing meetings and the word was he's sleeping, and then he's sleeping in the coaches' film sessions and he's not alert here. And he doesn't want to get to know the defense. I'm telling the defense, 'Hey, just trust me. You just got to give him time. He'll be fine.' And then he's telling me I don't need to get to know the defense at all," Rodgers said. There was also an eye-raising occurrence between the pair that happened during the Steelers' Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns on Oct. 1. Cameras caught Rodgers shouting toward the sideline and McCarthy appearing to mouth a profanity in response. -- Brooke Pryor and ESPN staff How was Rodgers playing before his release? Not well. Rodgers had the sixth-fastest time to throw in the league (2.85 seconds) with an astonishing 35% of his pass attempts not getting beyond the line of scrimmage (second in the league). He had the fourth-lowest success rate on pressured dropbacks and the fourth-lowest on-target rate on all dropbacks. He had disagreements with his receivers, as has been the case in recent years, and he was throwing low-probability heaves downfield to make a point when his pass catchers failed to separate. He saw the highest rate of man coverage this season (38.8%) of any quarterback of the past five seasons in large part because teams knew he wasn't accurate enough downfield to punish them for it. Rodgers' play was good enough -- he threw for 2,241 yards (17th in NFL) with 16 touchdowns (tied for 13th) -- that the Steelers could win six games despite his limitations. If this were only a football issue and not an interpersonal issue as well, he would not have been benched. But it is, and he was. -- Ben Solak If Rodgers is interested in playing again this season, which teams could make sense as fits? Rodgers' play this season hasn't been stellar. He just publicly torched his coach for 40 minutes on "The Pat McAfee Show" and would hijack any offense he takes over. He told McAfee that he demanded McCarthy relinquish playcalling or he wanted out of Pittsburgh. While there are teams with needs -- think of the Patriots, who just lost Drake Maye , and the Eagles, playing without Jalen Hurts -- it's hard to imagine any expressing interest. Yes, even at a minimum salary. The production (or lack thereof) does not offset the headache. Perhaps the rival Ravens, who play Pittsburgh twice down the stretch, would kick the tires, but that seems unlikely at this point. "Teams desperate on the playoff bubble, maybe, but it's going to be hard after watching him go scorched earth on people and an organization like that," an AFC team executive told ESPN. -- Jeremy Fowler What are the Steelers' cap ramifications for releasing the veteran QB? Likely none. Rodgers signed a simple one-year, $22,502,750 contract with the Steelers. Of that, $500,000 was a roster bonus (already paid), $2,750 was a workout bonus (already paid) and the remaining $22 million was a fully guaranteed salary, of which Rodgers has already made $13.44 million because he has been paid for the first 11 weeks of the 18-week regular season. Per the terms of the contract, the Steelers have to pay Rodgers the remaining $8.56 million because the salary was guaranteed, and his $22,502,750 cap number for 2026 will be unaffected. Given Rodgers' public comments, the Steelers could pursue a grievance against him for conduct detrimental to the team and try to get out of the remaining guaranteed money. If they do that and succeed, they will get the remaining $8.56 million refunded to them in the form of a salary cap credit at the end of this season. Remember, cap room can be carried forward from one year to the next. -- Dan Graziano What does this QB move mean for the Steelers' offense going forward? It means a couple of things. The first is that the Steelers are likely to run the ball more. Pittsburgh had the sixth-highest pass rate of all offenses this season (64%) and easily the highest of all offenses inside the 10-yard line (74%) -- in large part because Rodgers would audible the offense out of running plays and into his preferred dropbacks. This used to be one of his superpowers, but as defenses have improved disguises, Rodgers regularly hurt the offense by checking the unit into plays that didn't work against a disguised look post-snap. The Steelers' best avenue to team success -- both with and without Rodgers -- is leaning on their running backs ( Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle ) and defense to win low-scoring affairs. That will be the path going forward. The second: The Steelers are going to try to access the middle of the field more in the passing game. Only two quarterbacks threw less frequently to the intermediate range of the field (10-19 yards) than Rodgers because of how often he checked down quickly and how often he threw up prayerful heaves against one-on-ones. Mason Rudolph should have the arm and experience necessary to throw between the levels of the defense and create a more balanced passing attack. -- Solak Is there legitimacy to Rodgers' claims about McCarthy's past issues while with the Dallas Cowboys and Packers? McCarthy and Rodgers had a tense relationship during McCarthy's last season with the Packers in 2018, and I reported a story that went deep on their falling-out. That season, a source close to Rodgers told me that because McCarthy had other duties as the head coach, he regularly missed several offensive install meetings or quarterback meetings, which became a source of frustration for Rodgers because McCarthy would add or change plays during the Saturday walk-throughs that messed with the established flow of the game plan. "That drives Aaron crazy," the source close to Rodgers told me in 2018. "Especially over the years, [McCarthy] is not as present as he should be in meetings and all the game-planning." A former Green Bay staffer told me after Rodgers appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday that he remembers conversations with Rodgers in 2017 and 2018 in which the quarterback told him that McCarthy was missing meetings or falling asleep in them. The former Green Bay staffer said that based on those conversations, they were surprised that Rodgers signed back with Pittsburgh when the club hired McCarthy. Rodgers told McAfee that McCarthy doesn't watch as much film as he should as a playcaller. "Multiple times he said he hasn't watched the film when I've talked to him on Tuesdays," Rodgers said Wednesday. "He hasn't seen the film yet, hasn't seen the film yet. I don't know how that's possible on a Tuesday after you play on a Sunday." During McCarthy's first gap year in between jobs -- 2019 -- he set up a film lab in a barn to study football in depth with other retired and out-of-work coaches. In his introductory news conference in Dallas, McCarthy said he told Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones during the interview process that he watched every play of the 2019 NFL season, but when asked about this during the same event, McCarthy admitted he didn't actually do so. "I wanted the job," he said. -- Kalyn Kahler

stories.title: Rams' Kam Kinchens ejected as hit leaves Packers' Christian Watson concussed
stories.summary: Rams safety Kam Kinchens was ejected for a hit along the sideline that left Packers wide receiver Christian Watson with a concussion Wednesday night.
stories.detailText: INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- Los Angeles Rams safety Kam Kinchens was ejected for a hit along the sideline that left Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson with a concussion Wednesday night. The play came on a fourth-and-1 play late in the second quarter, when Kinchens left his feet and launched into Watson while leading with his head. Watson was down long enough that medical personnel came across the field with a gurney, but it was not needed. Watson got up and walked to the locker room. He was ruled out because of the concussion at the start of the second half. Kinchens initially was called for unnecessary roughness, then was ejected after a video review. He reached a maximum speed of 18.41 mph on the play, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Kinchens is the first Rams player disqualified from a game since Puka Nacua was ejected in Week 9 of the 2024 season against the Seattle Seahawks . Watson had four receptions for 65 yards and his career-best eighth touchdown of the season before exiting. Less than a month ago, he left the Week 8 game against the Carolina Panthers only to return later with a trip to the hospital in between. Tests showed Watson fractured a rib but suffered no other internal injuries, which is why he was cleared to return. ESPN's Rob Demovsky contributed to this report.

stories.title: Here's a roadmap to the Aaron Rodgers developments, one of the craziest stories in years
stories.summary: If you were traveling on Wednesday or otherwise not plugged in for one of the most rollicking, unpredictable days in years if not ever, you're in luck.
stories.detailText: If you were traveling on Wednesday or otherwise not plugged in for one of the most rollicking, unpredictable days in years if not ever, you're in luck. We've reconstructed the full timeline as to the events regarding now-former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers. It actually started on Monday, when coach Mike McCarthy was asked whether he has considered using one of the team's other three quarterbacks when the offense is struggling. McCarthy, whose body language in hindsight suggests he was dreading the question , said without equivocation, " Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback ." On Tuesday, Rodgers took his usual reps at practice. He conducted his usual midweek press conference. Unbeknownst to most of the media or the general public, the Steelers were changing their play-calling procedures to have quarterbacks coach Tom Arth, and not McCarthy, communicate the calls to Rodgers through the speaker in his helmet. Then came Tuesday night. At 11:10 p.m. ET, the Steelers issued a statement — not from coach Mike McCarthy or G.M. Omar Khan or owner Art Rooney II but from team spokesman Burt Lauten — that Mason Rudolph will start on Friday against the Broncos and Rodgers will be inactive. The news forced the Broncos to make a quick pivot in their preparations from Rodgers to Rudolph. As one source put it, the Broncos weren't sure whether it was a good thing or a bad thing . It was definitely a bad thing, all things considered, for the Steelers. By Wednesday morning, reports emerged that it was a coach’s decision . At 8:00 a.m. ET, McCarthy informed the team of the decision. Rodgers wasn’t there . As it turns out, he was excused . Enter Pat McAfee. He teased a surprise guest at 1:40 p.m. ET. As expected, it was Rodgers. Rodgers took a flamethrower to McCarthy, airing out dirty laundry that created a major mess for his now-former team. He exposed the fact that, at halftime of the Week 11 loss to the Eagles, McCarthy broke down the locker-room gathering by saying, " 1-2-3 Packers ." Rodgers also said McCarthy was falling asleep during some meetings and missing other meetings, expressing (in passive-aggressive fashion) concern for McCarthy's health. But Rodgers also said it was nothing new, and that McCarthy had done the same things in Green Bay, when they worked there together a decade ago. Rodgers also made it clear he wouldn't stay with the Steelers. After his session with McAfee and company, Dulac reported that the Steelers were expected to release Rodgers . By the official close of business, they’d waived him . A question lingers as to whether the Steelers will try to deny Rodgers the balance of his $22 million salary. It won't be easy; they'll need to both void the guarantees and wipe out his eligibility for termination pay (in the form of his remaining salary) under the Collective Bargaining Agreement. McCarthy met with reporters on Wednesday, after all hell had broken loose. He admitted to the "1-2-3 Packers" comment, calling it an " [e]mbarrassing moment ." McCarthy also said that Rodgers was benched after issuing an "ultimatum" that was " clearly outside of his job description ." ESPNFL thereafter reported that McCarthy " has the full support " of the organization, and that the team is "not planning to make any immediate changes." The key word may be "immediate"; with few viable options only two days before a Black Friday game against the Broncos, changes could come later. The overriding takeaway is that someone with the Steelers knew or should have known that McCarthy and Rodgers couldn't co-exist. Because, obviously, they didn't co-exist. If, as Rodgers claims, McCarthy believed Rodgers got him fired in Green Bay, McCarthy shouldn't have wanted a reunion with Rodgers. And if, as Rodgers claims, McCarthy was doing the same kinds of things in Green Bay that he did in Pittsburgh, Rodgers shouldn't have wanted a reunion with McCarthy. The reunion has now ended abruptly, with seven games left in the 2026 regular season. It remains to be seen whether Rodgers wants to play with another team, or whether another team wants him. Any team that signs him risks being on the receiving end of a future gripe session from Rodgers in which he lists all the things that team and/or the coach did wrong — without ever acknowledging his own role in the reality that it didn't work out. The good news, if there is any, is this: If Rodgers never plays again, his final NFL pass will have been a touchdown . Which is a better outcome than if he'd retired after the 2025 season. His final pass that year was a pick-six in the playoffs .

stories.title: NFL playoff picture Week 12: How Rams-Packers game impacts NFC field
stories.summary: Where the projected NFL playoff picture stands with Week 12 already underway.
stories.detailText: Every week for the duration of the 2026 regular season , USA TODAY Sports will provide timely updates to the NFL 's ever-evolving playoff picture − typically starting Sunday afternoon and then moving forward for the remainder of the week (through Monday's and Thursday's games or Saturday's, if applicable. And, when the holidays roll around, we'll be watching then, too). What just happened? What does it mean? What are the pertinent factors (and, perhaps, tiebreakers) prominently in play as each conference's seven-team bracket begins to crystallize? All will be explained and analyzed up to the point when the postseason field is finalized on Sunday, Jan. 10. Here's where things stand with Week 12 underway: AFC playoff picture 1. Buffalo Bills (9-1), AFC East leaders: Big game on Thanksgiving night as they try to take another step toward the home-field advantage they've never had during the Josh Allen era − but could secure in the first year they're in their glorious new stadium . The offense isn't firing on all cylinders right now, but the defense has been sublime lately ... albeit against mostly second-string QBs, who haven't engineered a TD drive against Buffalo since Nov. 1. Remaining schedule : vs. Chiefs, at Patriots, at Packers , vs. Bears , at Broncos , at Dolphins , vs. Jets 2. Denver Broncos (8-2), AFC West leaders: Seems like a lot is going their way, from the AFC's easiest remaining schedule to drawing the assignment against new Pittsburgh QB1 Mason Rudolph on Friday. A second straight No. 1 seed seems quite viable depending on how things unfold. They moved back atop the division Sunday thanks to their advantage in the common-games tiebreaker with the Chiefs − which pretty much boils down to Denver's OT defeat of Seattle. Remaining schedule : at Steelers, vs. Dolphins, at Jets, at Raiders, vs. Bills , at Patriots, vs. Chargers 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3), AFC South leaders: A roster reloaded ahead of the trade deadline and a weak division should keep the Jags on the fast track to a second straight divisional crown. But Sunday's loss to the Giants could sting as it pertains to a pursuit of the top seed. At least they regained a spot with Cincinnati's loss Monday night. Remaining schedule : vs. Titans, at Bears, vs. Steelers, at Texans , at Cowboys, vs. Commanders, at Colts 4. Cincinnati Bengals (7-3), AFC North leaders: Their divisional advantage dwindled to one game with Monday night's last-second loss and could be a major blow to any bid for the No. 1 seed. Still, Aaron Rodgers' departure in Pittsburgh further pronounces the gulf between QB Joe Burrow and his divisional counterparts. Remaining schedule : vs. Saints , at Browns, vs. Chiefs, at Panthers , at Colts, vs. Ravens , vs. Browns 5. Kansas City Chiefs (8-2), wild card No. 1: Doesn't help having the AFC's toughest schedule the rest of the way. And despite cruising past Arizona on Sunday, K.C. also lost its tiebreaker advantage over Denver for the time being. Remaining schedule : at Bills, at Rams, at Bengals , vs. Patriots, vs. 49ers , at Chargers, vs. Raiders 6. Cleveland Browns (6-4), wild card No. 2: Fruitful bye week as they moved up one spot in the seeding thanks to Pittsburgh's loss on the field ... to say nothing of the Steelers' disarray behind center. The Browns' superior AFC North record provides them an advantage over the Steelers, with whom they split their season series. Remaining schedule : vs. Raiders, vs. Bengals, vs. Falcons, at Giants, at Ravens, vs. Colts, vs. Bengals 7. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4), wild card No. 3: As if the Week 13 game against Houston didn't loom as potentially crucial for both squads, Friday should foretell how viable the Steelers are the rest of the way after the abrupt pivot at quarterback. Remaining schedule : vs. Broncos, vs. Texans, at Jaguars , vs. Ravens, vs. Panthers, at Titans, at Ravens NATE DAVIS: For Aaron Rodgers, his 'truth' is always worth burning things down 8. New England Patriots (5-5), in the hunt: They're without QB Drake Maye and running out of time to make a run, especially with the opponents they're about to face. Remaining schedule : at Chargers, vs. Bills, vs. Vikings, at Chiefs, at Jets, vs. Broncos, vs. Dolphins 9. Houston Texans (4-6), in the hunt: They moved up from 11th place after Week 11's rollover of the Colts . On the outer rim of the playoff fringe for weeks, the schedule should provide a pathway to relevance ... and maybe more. Remaining schedule : vs. Ravens, at Steelers, at Commanders, vs. Jaguars, at Eagles, at Packers, vs. Titans 10. Las Vegas Raiders (4-7), in the hunt: A superior conference record keeps them ahead of Baltimore. Remaining schedule : at Browns, BYE, vs. Chargers, vs. Broncos, vs. Titans, at Cardinals, at Chiefs 11. Baltimore Ravens (4-7), in the hunt: The chance they give QB Lamar Jackson a reason to return this season looks increasingly remote. Remaining schedule : at Texans, BYE, vs. Buccaneers , at Steelers, vs. Browns, at Bengals, vs. Steelers NFC playoff picture 1. San Francisco 49ers (9-1), NFC West leaders: They turned a highly anticipated matchup against Minnesota's vaunted defense into a rout − and hung on to the top seed last weekend, when the Niners were in jeopardy of losing it. Remaining schedule : vs. Seahawks , at Giants, vs. Rams, at Chargers, at Chiefs, vs. Eagles, at Cardinals 2. Detroit Lions (8-2) , NFC North leaders: Their first head-to-head meeting with the Bears on Thanksgiving will determine who's atop the division. Remaining schedule : vs. Bears, at Falcons, vs. Titans, at Vikings, vs. Giants, at Bears, at Packers 3. New York Giants (6-3-1), NFC East leaders: They have the most difficult remaining schedule in their division . But they knocked off Jacksonville on Sunday, and the Cowboys have yet to prove they can take advantage of their opportunities to gain ground this season. Remaining schedule : at Colts, vs. 49ers, at Seahawks, vs. Browns, at Lions, at Cowboys, vs. Eagles 4. Carolina Panthers (5-5), NFC South leaders: By squeaking past the Ravens on Sunday, they opened up a two-game lead on the rest of the division. But getting swept by Tampa Bay would cost them ground and a massive tiebreaker. Remaining schedule : at Buccaneers, at Vikings, vs. Saints, vs. Bengals, at Steelers, vs. Seahawks, at Falcons 5. Chicago Bears (8-2) , wild card No. 1: They picked up a spot in the seeding thanks to Minnesota's loss Sunday. Next up, first place in the NFC North? Remaining schedule : at Lions, vs. Jaguars, at Dolphins, at Bills, vs. Packers, vs. Lions, at Vikings 6. Minnesota Vikings (7-3), wild card No. 2: Kirk Cousins' return was a smashing success ... after one game. Sunday's loss to the Niners south of the border was a systemic disaster that could call the Vikes' Super Bowl bona fides into question. Remaining schedule : vs. Falcons, vs. Panthers, at Patriots, vs. Lions, vs. Commanders, at Jets, vs. Bears 7. Green Bay Packers (6-4), wild card No. 3: Is this really going to be the fourth straight season they finish as the NFC's final wild-card entry? A 4-4 record in NFC games currently confers the tiebreaker over Seattle, which is 2-3 in that department. Beat the Rams Wednesday, and the Pack hang on to the seventh seed. If not, they drop from the field. Remaining schedule : at Rams, at Saints, vs. Bills, vs. Dolphins, at Bears, vs. Texans, vs. Lions 8. Seattle Seahawks (6-4), in the hunt: The defending champs have been beset by various issues − a new offensive coordinator, a series of QB injuries, having to use their entire running back depth chart. If most of those resolve, maybe they can ultimately break through the NFC North logjam ahead of them. More immediately, they need to stave off a season sweep by the Niners on Sunday afternoon. Remaining schedule : at 49ers, vs. Cowboys, vs. Giants, at Eagles, vs. Rams, at Panthers, at Rams 9. Los Angeles Rams (6-4), in the hunt: Losing their first two NFC West games further hinders a team that's failed to live up to its own hype this season. The Rams also own the league's second-toughest remaining schedule ... and won't have suspended/injured WR Puka Nacua back this season. Regardless, win Wednesday, and they jump into the projected field. Remaining schedule : vs. Packers, vs. Chiefs, at 49ers, vs. Cowboys, at Seahawks, at Buccaneers, vs. Seahawks 10. Dallas Cowboys (5-6), in the hunt: Convincing victory Sunday against Tennessee . (Yawn.) But winning the NFC East is probably Dallas' only hope of making the field. Remaining schedule : vs. Eagles, at Seahawks, BYE, at Rams, vs. Jaguars, vs. Giants, at Commanders 11. Washington Commanders (4-5-1), in the hunt: They're stacking wins and wading into increasingly advantageous circumstances that might just pave the road to the top of the NFC East . Remaining schedule : at Cardinals, at Titans, vs. Texans, vs. Falcons, at Vikings, at Jaguars, vs. Cowboys All the NFL news on and off the field. Sign up for USA TODAY's 4th and Monday newsletter . stories.detailText: Former CBS NFL analyst Tony Romo has taken a job with Betr, a sports gambling company co-founded by Jake Paul. Romo announced the move Wednesday, less than two months after he and CBS parted ways. Betr said the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback would make predictions and engage with fans across the company's platforms. CBS placed Romo on leave after his July 23 arrest in Wisconsin on charges of operating a vehicle while intoxicated, and the network and Romo later agreed that he would not return. Romo, 46 pleaded no contest to the citation. According to Milwaukee County court records, Romo lost his driving privileges for six months and was ordered to complete an alcohol assessment program. He made four Pro Bowl appearances during a playing career that ran from 2004 to 2016 and was spent entirely with Dallas. Romo spent nine seasons as CBS' lead NFL analyst. The network replaced him with J.J. Watt.

stories.title: The Aaron Rodgers ultimatum that sent the Steelers into chaos
stories.summary: It all started with a Tuesday meeting between the coach and QB, who won a Super Bowl together in 2011 with the Packers.
stories.detailText: Mike McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers speak on the sidelines as the Steelers face the Bengals. Aaron Rodgers ended up on the wrong side of his own ultimatum. The now-former Steelers quarterback was waived by the team on Wednesday, following a wild 18-hour period that saw him get benched in a late-night announcement and then go nuclear on coach Mike McCarthy in a nationally televised tirade. It all started with a Tuesday meeting between the coach and QB, who won a Super Bowl together in 2011 with the Packers. “I didn’t want this to be the way that it ended,” Rodgers said in an explosive appearance on the “Pat McAfee Show” on Wednesday. “But I was very clear with the ultimatum and it wasn’t a veiled ultimatum. It wasn’t posturing. It was me as a leader of the football team inspired by my teammates who talk about this all the time. Literally all the time in council meetings, on group chats, in the locker room, just some of the things that are just like wow, how is this the reality we’re dealing with? I was, in my professional opinion based on 22 years of experience … the only person who could talk to him and be honest with him to tell him that what’s best for the team is for him to not call the plays and if he wasn’t up for that, they should probably release me.” According to Netflix NFL insider Tom Pelissero , McCarthy was open to Rodgers’ demand, as the veteran has been calling plays himself in recent weeks, but other coaches and “some in the locker room” convinced him it was not a move they wanted. McCarthy confirmed in a press conference later in the day that Rodgers attempted to put the screws to him. Mike McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers speak on the sidelines as the Steelers face the Bengals. Getty Images “We got to a point, we talked some things — you know communication and things like that — and there was an ultimatum made clearly outside of his job description and so it was my decision to bench him,” McCarthy told reporters . McCarthy made the call to move backup Mason Rudolph into the starter’s role, kicking off a chaotic day in which Rodgers accused his coach of falling asleep in meetings and divulging a halftime gaffe in which he said, “1-2-3 Packers!” among other things. Pittsburgh players reportedly watched Rodgers burn it all down on McAfee’s live ESPN broadcast on their phones in the locker room in real time. Hours later, the team granted the soon-to-be 43-year-old quarterback his ultimatum and sent him packing.

stories.title: Buccaneers will need more from Baker Mayfield and struggling passing attack to beat the Panthers
stories.summary: — The Tampa Bay Buccaneers didn't need much from Baker Mayfield to rout the Carolina Panthers last month.
stories.detailText: TAMPA, Fla. -- — The Tampa Bay Buccaneers didn't need much from Baker Mayfield to rout the Carolina Panthers last month. Winning without a viable passing attack wasn't sustainable, however. Mayfield threw just 11 passes in a 43-13 victory at Carolina on Oct. 25. He didn't even complete a pass in a 16-0 win over Atlanta the following week. But the run game could only get them so far. Tampa Bay has lost two in a row heading into a key matchup Monday night against the Panthers. Mayfield threw a critical pick-6 in a loss to Chicago and had 187 yards passing and two TDs in a loss at Detroit. The NFC South standings will be clear after this one. The Panthers (5-5) would move closer to a second straight division title with a victory. A win would put the Buccaneers (3-7) within one game of first place with a tiebreaker advantage over Carolina. “It’s been a frustrating year, but on the other side of it, everything we want is still in front of us,” Mayfield said. "So, it’s (about) how can you handle it and get better, not waste any reps, the preparation, how can you do that the best as possible and prepare to take it one game at a time.” Mayfield is 6-1 against the Panthers since they cut him during the 2022 season. He revived his career in Tampa Bay in 2023 with Dave Canales , who spent one season as the offensive coordinator before going to Carolina. “When you look at the last game they didn't ask him to throw it a bunch. But the ones that he did, they were impactful," Canales said. “There was a scramble red zone play where he found a touchdown. ... Baker finds ways to get out of that arm tackle. That has to be an emphasis for our guys to lower their target.” Carolina's loss to Tampa Bay sparked a three-game losing streak. But the Panthers have responded with back-to-back wins against New Orleans and Baltimore to take control of the NFL's weakest division. The Falcons and Saints are also 3-7. Bryce Young led the go-ahead score in the fourth quarter last week to beat the Ravens 35-33. “Game on the line, there’s nobody else I want with the ball,” Canales said. “Bryce Young is going to go there. He’s going to be in control. He’s going to be focused and locked into the moment, and that’s what he looked like on that drive.” The Panthers have a two-game lead over the rest of the division for the first time since the end of the 2015 season — the year they last went to the Super Bowl. A win over the Bucs would give Carolina at least one win over all three teams in the NFC South. Panthers linebacker Devin Lloyd acknowledged this is a golden opportunity to put some distance between them and the Bucs and even the head-to-head tiebreaker, but added “ultimately it’s about going 1-0 this week.” Need to know Carolina (5-5) at Tampa Bay (3-7). When/where to watch: Monday, 8:15 p.m., EST, ESPN. Latest odds: Buccaneers by 3 Against the spread: Buccaneers 4-6, Panthers 4-6. Last week: Buccaneers lost to the Lions 31-21; Panthers beat Ravens 35-33. Last meeting: Buccaneers beat Panthers 43-13 on Oct. 25 in Charlotte, North Carolina. Series tied 26-26. Matchup to watch Buccaneers RB Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell vs. Panthers front seven. Irving carried 24 times for 106 yards and two touchdowns and Gainwell added 14 rushes for 88 yards as the Bucs piled up 258 yards on the ground in a 43-13 blowout win over the Panthers last month. Less than two weeks later, the Panthers fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and promoted defensive line coach Todd Wash on an interim basis. Carolina has been better in the past three games against the run, although the did allow Derrick Henry and Justice Hill to combine for 163 yards and two touchdowns on 19 carries last Sunday. “The big message this week for us to be gap sound and tackle better,” Panthers defensive lineman Derrick Brown said. “Gainwell and Bucky, they are still rolling. Last week they had a few long runs called back (because of penalties). Those guys can go east and west and fast as they can go north and south.” Stats and stuff — The Panthers have not won at Raymond James Stadium since 2017. — RB Chuba Hubbard has carried 54 times for 212 yards and four touchdowns in the past two weeks. He ranks fourth among all running backs in scrimmage yards (1,078) and is tied for fifth in scrimmage touchdowns (11). — Young has 14 career game-winning drives, the second most among all quarterbacks since 2023 and tied with Justin Herbert and Dak Prescott for the most by a quarterback under the age of 26 in the Super Bowl era. — Carolina’s tight ends combined are tied for third in the league in receptions per game (7.1) and touchdowns receiving per game (0.8) and rank fourth in yards receiving per game (80.1). — The Panthers have committed 93 penalties that have been accepted by their opponent, the most in the league. — The Bucs have won 11 of the past 13 meetings. — Mayfield has thrown a TD pass in 18 of his past 19 primetime games. — Irving has 1,031 scrimmage yards (893 rush, 138 receiving) this season. — WR Emeka Egbuka needs four catches to reach 100 career receptions. — LB Josiah Trotter ranks fifth among rookies with 84 tackles. — Bucs are 2-10 in primetime games with Mayfield. ------ Reed reported from Charlotte, North Carolina. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Blake Corum receives a heartwarming birthday surprise from his family moments before Thanksgiving Eve game
stories.summary: Blake Corum receives a surprise from his family ahead of a Thanksgiving game.The Los Angeles Rams and Green Bay Packers are about to play in the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game,...
stories.detailText: Blake Corum receives a surprise from his family ahead of a Thanksgiving game. The Los Angeles Rams and Green Bay Packers are about to play in the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game, and the calendar just happened to have it land on Blake Corum’s birthday. While Corum took the field at SoFi Stadium for pregame warmups, the Rams running back had a moment he’ll never forget. Blake Corum running past a Giants defender in an NFL game. Charles Wenzelberg/New York Post Corum was seen walking toward the end zone and was surprised by members of his family who showed up wearing matching sweaters that included Corum’s face while he was wearing a birthday party hat on his head. Corum’s family members were also holding individual signs that matched the face on their sweaters to show their support for the Rams running back. Before the Rams went on the bye week last week, Corum had his best performance of the season, when he was the Rams’ leading rusher in their 34-6 win against the Cardinals. Blake Corum celebrating a play during an NFL game. AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough Los Angeles ran the ball for 202 yards, and Corum was their lead running back, carrying the ball 17 times for 100 yards and a touchdown. Corum is in his rookie season in the NFL and has shared lead bell-cow duties with Kyren Williams. The duo has nearly matched each other’s production entirely this year, as they’ve combined for 1,163 yards and 11 touchdowns. Blake Corum running past a Washington Commanders defender during an NFL game. Getty Images Corum comes into Wednesday’s game, scoring a touchdown in four consecutive games. The two will have a tough load to face against Green Bay, as they will be without starting and backup centers, Coleman Shelton and Dylan McMahon, who are both on the injured reserve . The woes of the Rams’ offensive line also came when the Packers announced that three-time edge rusher Micah Parsons would be activated from the team’s injured reserve. The Rams and Packers will kick off at 5:15 p.m. and will be streaming live on Netflix.

stories.title: Seahawks-49ers Wednesday injury report: Sam Darnold practices fully
stories.summary: Five players were sidelined in Seattle’s first practice of the week, but Sam Darnold practiced in full.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) | Getty Images Coming off two consecutive wins and their bye, there’s plenty working in favor of the Seattle Seahawks as they head into a pivotal matchup against the NFC-leading San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, but Wednesday’s injury report wasn’t exactly promising. Seahawks Nov. 25 practice report Did not participate: LB Demarcus Lawrence (shoulder) OT Abraham Lucas (ankle) QB Jalen Milroe (illness) OG Quenton Nelson (knee) DT Jarran Reed (toe) Limited participant: OG Anthony Bradford (knee, illness) QB Drew Lock (right elbow) OT Charles Cross (ankle) LB Ernest Jones IV (knee) TE Nick Kallerup (ankle) WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) DT Leonard Williams (stinger) Full participant QB San Darnold (quadricep, ribs) LB Patrick O’Connell (toe) With the status of backups quarterbacks Drew Lock and Jalen Milroe up in the air, a full practice for Sam Darnold certainly bodes well for his return to come against the 49ers. During Monday’s press conference, head coach Mike Macdonald refused to make any officials declarations regarding the Super Bowl winning quarterback, but said Wednesday’s practice would be a big indicator of whether he’d be able to suit up, and it appears he’s trending in the right direction. Macdonald has not yet confirmed Darnold as the starter, but stated he remains the team’s go-to guy when healthy and a quarterback change is not being contemplated. Although Lock’s right elbow tendinitis has lingered since October, he’s suited up the past two weeks and his limited practice merely appears cautionary. Regarding Milroe, whether he’s able to particpant in any capacity over the next two days will likely determine his availability against San Francisco, but the team has recently signed QB Adrian Martinez on their practice squad should he be sidelined this weekend. Regardless of who’s under center, they’ll face an additional challenge with OG Quenton Nelson and OT Abraham Lucas ruled out, a move announced by Macdonald this afternoon . Josh Jones is set to draw the start in place of Lucas, with Anthony Bradford in line to suit up at right guard — if he’s cleared. Despite having played in Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders, the fourth-year pro was limited with a knee injury that forced him to practice in a limited capacity leading up to the game, and it appears to still be lingering. Bradford previously missed five weeks while on injured reserve as he dealt with a knee injury originally suffered in Week 2. Should he be unable to go, rookie Beau Stephens would be in line to draw the start. Arguably the two most troublesome absences’ are that of DT Jarran Reed and LB Demarcus Lawrence. Reed originally suffered a toe injury against the Raiders but later returned to the game. It remains unknown if the team’s decision to hold him out is cautionary or because it worsened, but his status tomorrow will definitely be an indicator for Sunday. As for Lawrence, there hadn’t been an indication he was dealing with an injury and the severity of it remains unclear. Although DT Leonard Williams’ limited practice is an improvement, WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba and LB Ernest Jones IV not participant in a full capacity is alarming. However, the veteran linebacker previously popped up on Seattle’s practice report for Week 3 and 9 with separate injuries and went on to play — so his status downgrade shouldn’t be flagged just yet. The same goes for Smith-Njigba, who was flagged for an ankle injury prior to the Seahawks’ Week 6 game against the Denver Broncos and went on to play without an injury designation. Further updates should come tomorrow, when Seattle holds their second practice of the week practice of the week and they’ll will release their official injury designation on Friday.

stories.title: Myles Garrett won’t be ‘100%’ for remainder of season
stories.summary: Cleveland Browns defensive end Myles Garrett will not be 100 percent healthy for the remainder of the season.Myles Garrett is back to playing football in a Rams uniform for the...
stories.detailText: Cleveland Browns defensive end Myles Garrett will not be 100 percent healthy for the remainder of the season. Myles Garrett is back to playing football in a Rams uniform for the third game in a row, but there is concern about what his long-term health will look like. “It is unrealistic to think he will be 100% or even 90% this season,” NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported. “There is no looking back — he expects to keep ramping up his role,” Pelissero said of Garrett. The latest from @TomPelissero on news around the @NFL including Aaron Rodgers, Micah Parsons and Myles Garrett. Josh Jacobs will be OUT tonight for the Packers. Packers vs. Rams — LIVE now on Netflix pic.twitter.com/OOHev59EUC — Netflix Sports (@netflixsports) November 25, 2026 Myles Garrett coming on the field during an NFL game. Getty Images Garrett spoke more in depth about his injury on “The Rich Eisen Show” earlier this month and talked about how it is hard to come back “100% in the middle of a season.” “I was expecting to come back in a position where I wasn’t going to do any further damage to my own health and longevity, but I could have a positive impact for my team and my teammates,” Garrett said. “And that’s fortunately what I was able to do my first game back.” The concern for Garrett’s health came after he suffered a knee injury during their Week 1 loss to the 49ers in Melbourne, Australia. Garrett played 40 snaps against San Francisco and rotated in and out of the team’s defensive line. He finished the game with no tackles, sacks or quarterback hits. Myles Garrett greeting a member of the Washington Commanders after an NFL game. Getty Images The Rams’ top offseason acquisition spent most of training camp sidelined due to knee soreness but played through it during the 49ers game. Once the Rams returned from Australia, Garrett headed to the team’s injured list and needed arthroscopic knee surgery, keeping him sidelined until Week 9 when they played the Commanders. Myles Garrett sacking Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels in his first NFL game back from arthroscopic surgery. AP Photo/Nick Wass Garrett was expected to play about 25 snaps in his first game back, but he ended up exceeding that goal and played 35 of the Rams’ 58 defensive plays. His first game back was a statement performance, compiling three sacks and a forced fumble against Washington.

stories.title: Abdul Carter demanding more from himself after breakout may be key to Giants ‘super challenging’ Colts task
stories.summary: After a 12-pressure breakout game, Giants outside linebacker Abdul Carter aims to keep his momentum going against new Colts starter Anthony Richardson.
stories.detailText: If Bruce Springsteen’s go-to encore performance is “Born to Run,” maybe Abdul Carter’s can be “Born to Run Down QBs.” Carter, who did not practice Wednesday with the Giants because of a supposedly minor calf/ankle injury, raised the bar of possibilities Sunday with a breakout game (12 quarterback pressures, five quarterback hits and two sacks) followed by his self-description as “the best in the world.” Access the Giants like never before Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers. tRY IT NOW So, what does the freshly named NFC Defensive Player of the Week have in store Sunday against the Colts and new starting quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr.? “Something I said to the team during training camp: What this sport is all about each week is having to prove and re-prove, so gotta do it again,” Carter said. “I could’ve done a lot better — get a couple more sacks — but we’ll see.” More? “I think I can be the greatest,” Carter said, “so I’m going to keep chasing that.” The Giants are going to be chasing Richardson, who will be making his first start since Dec. 22, 2024. The 244-pound tackle-breaker is more dangerous on designed runs (RPOs, zone reads and even option keepers with Jonathan Taylor as a decoy) than drop-back passes (career 50.6 percent completion rate). Abdul Carter reacts during the Giants’ win over the Jaguars on Nov. 22, 2026, at MetLife Stadium. Getty Images “I think we have an opportunity to leave a mark this week, earn another ‘W,’ extend our lead [in the NFC East],” said Carter, who declared himself “fine” for game day. “I attack each week the same way. Every team is different. But I’m going to prepare the same way I did last week — and do a little bit more.” The Colts reinstalled Richardson — a 2023 first-round draft bust — as their quarterback after surprisingly cutting Daniel Jones , who started the first 11 games. “They are going to do things to make sure the game comes to him easily so he can get in a rhythm,” safety Jevón Holland said. “His running style is like a Cam Newton — using his size to his advantage, stiff-arms, putting his shoulder down and getting extra yards. It’s a challenge playing a quarterback with that size and speed.” The Colts quarterback change threw the Giants a “super challenging” curveball similar to Week 9, when they faced dual-threat Joe Milton III in his Eagles debut, head coach John Harbaugh said. “It’s a little better to see him the second game because you kind of see what they’ve got in for him,” Harbaugh said. “We won’t have the advantage of knowing what particular plays they choose to run. “We watched all of his cut-ups — about 700 plays of his NFL career. He’s one of a kind — a rare athlete. His career hasn’t taken off for whatever reason, but that talent’s there. He’s going to be looking forward to his opportunity to prove himself, as is their whole team, so we’re taking it very seriously.” Six of Carter’s 12 pressures against the Jaguars came in less than 2.5 seconds, bringing his season total to 23 quick pressures (ranked No. 3 in the NFL). It certainly looked like he had a bead on the snap count, which spells trouble for a Colts offensive line pieced together after injuries and trade departures. “That was crazy,” 10-year veteran defensive lineman Dawuane Smoot, Carter’s teammate for the last month, told The Post. “The amount of focus he had during the week, and I don’t know what tip he had on that ball because he still hasn’t even told us.” Smoot has played with future Hall of Famer Von Miller and Pro Bowler Josh Hines-Allen. What is Carter’s ceiling? Anthony Richardson Sr. throws a pass during the Colts’ blowout loss to the Texans on Nov. 19, 2026, at Reliant Stadium in Houston. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect “You can’t really put a name on it,” Smoot said. “He could be the greatest of all time. He has the confidence to be able to get there.” Richardson is trying to speak into existence salvaging his career. He will challenge the Giants safeties by dragging them up in support but using his big arm to throw over their heads. “We’re ball-conscious at all times,” said Holland, who has four of the Giants’ 10 interceptions. “He hasn’t played, so we don’t really know what his accuracy levels are. I’m going to expect him to deliver the ball and play my keys as such.” Unless, of course, Carter’s pressure blows up the timing of plays again. “If we are who we say we are,” Carter said, “we have to … stop the run and earn the right to rush the passer.”

stories.title: Five Plays: Pitt First Quarter
stories.summary: Tre Richardson gets the highlight on this play, but look at the blocking from the receivers on the outside. This group of players came in for this play and then exited the game. Deion Branch and Brian Brohm have a distinct package for these guys, which should be worn as a badge of honor. Good […]
stories.detailText: Louisville’s Tre Richardson got a first down and a little more against Pittsburg at L&N Field Stadium. Nov. 21, 2026 | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Tre Richardson gets the highlight on this play, but look at the blocking from the receivers on the outside. This group of players came in for this play and then exited the game. Deion Branch and Brian Brohm have a distinct package for these guys, which should be worn as a badge of honor. Good on Richardson to make the one unblocked guy miss, but this is a great team effort to make a big play. Demeco Kennedy had his best game on Saturday, and his best plays did not show up on the stat sheet. He gets great penetration on this play with a really nice move to get skinny and then rip through the left guard. You can see how he uses his left arm to rip upwards, which leaves the blocker with nothing to latch on to, and it gets Kennedy up the field right into the path of the running back. He doesn’t make the tackle on this play, but he makes the play. It hasn’t happened every week, but it’s just about every week that Lincoln Kienholz doesn’t throw a quick pass with pressure coming at him, and he takes a sack. Tre Richardson is about as open as a receiver can be, and it looks to me that Kienholz is looking through him, waiting for Lawayne McCoy to come open on a deeper route. He has to consistently take what is given and let his very talented skill guys make plays for him. This was the longest play of the game for Pitt, and it provided a nice teaching moment for Antonio Harris who earned his first start of his career. UofL is in a basic Cover 3 with Harris giving a good amount of space to Blue Hicks. At the snap, Harris does well to get depth so that he can ensure Hicks doesn’t run by him. Where Harris makes a mistake is that he doesn’t get depth to the boundary in his drop. Hicks is angling outside before he cuts on this out route. Harris has to match him in his drop as opposed to going straight backwards in his backpedal. Because he doesn’t do that, he is much further away from Hicks than he wants to be when he makes this catch. He can’t make a play on this ball, and then he misses the tackle, in part, because he’s scrambling to get to him instead of being under control. A good play for him to learn from as he hopefully gets more playing time. Louisville had a safety behind the receiver on a deep route. Pretty nice. It’s actually very interesting to see how they played this. It looks like Cover 3 to me, but Kaleb Beasley immediately shades towards the numbers to the top of the screen. He essentially locks in on the receiver at the top of the screen. I wonder if this is a Cover 3 look that is really a quarters-type shell zone. Antonio Harris bails into a deep zone towards the hash at the snap, even though there is an outside receiver running a go route. Seems like a new wrinkle in the defense. I believe they gave the credit for this forced fumble to TJ Capers, but it looks clear to me that Tommy Zeismer poked the ball out as the running back tried to run by him. It’s a really impressive play, mostly because he’s battling hard to hold the point of attack here before he gets his arm out to knock the ball out. The havoc plays behind the line of scrimmage are great, but just going to battle with a blocker and not being pushed out of the play is valuable for a defensive lineman. At the very least, he is getting in on a tackle here for maybe a 3-yard gain. Your weekly installment of Lincoln Kienholz doing something we haven’t seen in years from a Louisville quarterback is here. There will be more.

stories.title: Kyren Williams makes it 13-3 Rams in second quarter
stories.summary: The Rams have had the ball three times and all three drives have ended in points.
stories.detailText: The Rams have had the ball three times and all three drives have ended in points. Running back Kyren Williams finished off the third possession with a seven-yard sprint into the end zone that pushed the Rams' lead over the Packers to 13-3 with 11:29 to play in the first half. It's the first time the Rams have scored on their first three possessions this season and it's also the first time the Packers have allowed their opponents points on their first three drives. Most of the other movement on the drive came through the air. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford completed passes to Williams, tight end Davis Allen, wide receiver Konata Mumpfield, and tight end Tyler Higbee for first downs before Williams's touchdown. The throw to Williams came just before Stafford took a hit from Packers defensive end Micah Parsons. Stafford is 10-of-12 for 87 yards while Jordan Love is 6-of-10 for 70 yards, including a 32-yarder to Christian Watson that set up Trey Smack's 54-yard field goal.

stories.title: Aaron Rodgers' comments on 'The Pat McAfee Show' draw NFL reaction
stories.summary: The now-former Steelers quarterback made a number of noteworthy comments in a bombshell interview on "The Pat McAfee Show" Wednesday afternoon.
stories.detailText: Aaron Rodgers ' explosive interview Wednesday on "The Pat McAfee Show" following his stunning benching late Tuesday night sent shock waves across the NFL and social media. The four-time NFL MVP accused Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy of various things, including sleeping through meetings, breaking a huddle with "one, two, three, Packers " and not watching film. His nearly 40-minute appearance on McAfee's show was followed by the Steelers officially releasing Rodgers. Rodgers returned to Pittsburgh after its January hiring of McCarthy, the coach alongside whom Rodgers won a Super Bowl in 2011. McCarthy served as Packers head coach from 2006 to 2018, when he was fired after Week 13. Rodgers vouched for his former coach to be interviewed by Pittsburgh, believing it would be different this time. However, it wasn't, and Rodgers aired it all out on McAfee's show Wednesday, ripping McCarthy at the same time as Pittsburgh held a practice. His comments prompted widespread reaction on social media, from former Steelers and beyond. A two-time Super Bowl champion with the Steelers, James Harrison didn't deny what Rodgers accused McCarthy of. Former Harrison teammate Ryan Clark expressed the same message and defended his former coach, Mike Tomlin. Meanwhile, J.J. Watt, whose brother T.J. Watt plays for Pittsburgh, had a clever post after touching down in Detroit.

stories.title: Is Aaron Rodgers right? QB raises questions Mike McCarthy, Steelers must answer | Opinion
stories.summary: Aaron Rodgers didn't sound as if he was lying. If he's not, than the Pittsburgh Steelers need to get Mike McCarthy help.
stories.detailText: What if Aaron Rodgers is telling the truth about Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy ? Or enough of it? Yes, Rodgers is a master manipulator , someone who has had no trouble lying when it suited his purposes or made him look better. He’s also a conspiracy theorist, suckered by some truly outlandish theories that most other people saw right through. But what if he’s right? It’s easy to dismiss Rodgers’ scorched earth takedown of Mike McCarthy on Wednesday, Nov. 25, as Rodgers being Rodgers, finally settling scores that have been festering for more than a decade and making an exit in such incendiary fashion it will loom large in NFL lore for years to come. But, again, what if he’s right? When Rodgers has lied before, be it about COVID or Jimmy Kimmel , he’s danced around the edges, getting too cute by half with double talk and innuendos. He didn’t do that with McCarthy. He was specific in the dates and details of how McCarthy was derelict in his duties, down to the coach shuffling papers when he woke up during a Nov. 18 quarterbacks meeting before quickly falling asleep again. And Rodgers, for his many, many faults, is not a dumb man. He has to know that disparaging McCarthy as specifically as he did could bring legal action, or at least the threat of it, if he doesn’t have corroboration. More: For Aaron Rodgers, his 'truth' is always worth burning things down | Opinion Steelers have obligation to fans, Mike McCarthy if Aaron Rodgers is right So, what if he’s right? The Steelers have an obligation to their fans, obviously, and McCarthy’s lethargic news conference a few hours after Rodgers’ bombshell isn’t going to cut it. Especially when McCarthy did little to dispute Rodgers’ most stunning accusation, that the coach mistook the Steelers for a team he last coached in 2018 when he said “1, 2, 3, Packers ” during a halftime speech in that dispiriting loss to Philadelphia. "The Philadelphia situation at halftime was very emotional," McCarthy said when asked about it directly. "There's conversations prior to that. Embarrassing moment, but I just think we work a lot of hours, so definitely a difference of opinion from what I was told about the comments." That’s not a “No.” That’s not an “I never said that.” If Rodgers is lying, in ways large or small, someone from the organization needs to state that unequivocally. Whether it’s Pittsburgh general manager Omar Khan or owner Art Rooney II, somebody has to go chapter and verse through what Rodgers said and explain why it’s not true. Bring receipts, too. Because if Rodgers isn’t lying, if he’s right about any of it, then McCarthy needs help. Now. 'You're unwell' Allowing him to coach the rest of the season would not only be a betrayal of the Steelers and their very loyal fanbase, it would be a betrayal of McCarthy himself. Not as a coach. As a human being. Relieving him of playcalling duties or handing off the walkthroughs to his coordinators won’t cut it. The Steelers would need to bench McCarthy until he gets the medical attention that he needs. “There’s no hyperbole, there’s no trying to stick it to you. You’re unwell,” Rodgers said he told McCarthy. "This has been a conversation for weeks and weeks and weeks. And every time I bring these things up, he just denies it,” Rodgers added. “There's been other individuals who've talked to him about some of these habits, and he just shoots off at it and gets super angry and goes into getting after the person bringing it and not the actual content of what's going on. “It’s been frustrating,” Rodgers said. “… I came to him many, many times to try and help him.” Again, it's easy to write off Rodgers' accusations as another chapter in his book of grievances. Lord knows there's enough of those. He also glossed over the fact that his declining play is why the Steelers are in free fall, losers of their last two ahead of a game against the Denver Broncos on Friday, Nov. 27. But it was telling that there was no snarkiness from Rodgers as he talked, no smirk that suggested he thought he was pulling one over on everyone. He was upset, yes, angry that McCarthy would disrespect the game in this way. Mostly, though, he was somber, seemingly pained both that things had gotten this far and for his role in it. “I continued a pattern I did for most of my career with him: I protected him. I didn’t talk about the things publicly. I didn’t talk about his habits,” Rodgers said. Now that he has, it leaves only one question: What if he's right? Follow USA TODAY Sports columnist Nancy Armour on social media @nrarmour. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Is Aaron Rodgers right? stories.summary: Cam Skattebo has bigger things to play for than showing Jonathan Taylor he is good enough to keep Taylor away from the Giants.
stories.detailText: Cam Skattebo has bigger things to play for than showing Jonathan Taylor he is good enough to keep Taylor away from the Giants . Access the Giants like never before Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers. tRY IT NOW “He’s on a 3-7 team; I’m on a 6-3 team. So it’s a little different the way they are doing things over there and the way we are doing things over here,” Skattebo said Wednesday, with preparations underway to face Taylor’s Colts. “I have to play my game. I have to play the game the coaches want me to play and my teammates need me to play. I’m not really looking to impress anybody else on the other side or show them I can do it more than them.” The Giants offered a second- and fifth-round pick for Taylor, 27, at the trade deadline, but the Colts declined. Cam Skattebo warms up before the Giants’ win over the Jaguars on Nov. 22, 2026, at MetLife Stadium. AP Photo/Frank Franklin II It doesn’t mean the sides can’t revisit negotiations in the offseason, when the next Colts general manager begins his rebuild and wants younger assets. “Jonathan Taylor is one of the premier backs … for a reason,” coach John Harbaugh said. “He’s a slasher. I call him a ‘crease hitter.’ They run the stretch-and-cut type of an idea. He can put his foot in the ground and he can accelerate and change angles real fast. He runs behind his pads. He’ll bounce it or cut it back all the way in both directions. He’s a threat in the passing game. He can pass protect. All-around player.” Skattebo hasn’t done his job security any favors with five fumbles on 147 touches this season. But, unlike when he was benched for a game after fumble No. 4 , the Giants handed it to Skattebo to run out the clock with a first down Sunday after fumble No. 5. “I’m here for a reason,” Skattebo said. “I’ll be here for a long time.” Was it a vote of confidence from Harbaugh? Or an act of desperation? Jonathan Taylor jogs off the field after the Colts’ blowout loss to the Texans on Nov. 19, 2026, in Houston. Getty Images “The fact that they are trusting me in that moment and coming back to me, it was huge for me and my confidence being able to get the ball again,” Skattebo said. “I don’t want to say it, but when you’re the last resource — you’ve got a guy hurt [Tyrone Tracy Jr.] and me and ‘Motor’ [Devin Singletary] on the field — and the other guys are more of the special-teams guys, he looked at me and said, ‘You have no choice but to go run the damn ball.’ I was in there and I was ready for it.” Taylor was not asked about the Giants’ trade interest Wednesday in Indianapolis. Skattebo’s past two games have been the highest snap share of his two-year career (both over 84 percent). He told Harbaugh to keep feeding him. “If I’m the guy they want to play 80 percent of the snaps, I have to be ready for it and I have to take care of the ball,” Skattebo said. “This run game is going to explode. It just takes time, and it’s going to find its way.” OLB Abdul Carter (ankle/calf), DT Shelby Harris (illness) and CB Dru Phillips (illness) did not practice. TE Isaiah Likely (groin) and LB Arvell Reese (back) were limited.

teamStories.summary: — Deshaun Watson and Fernando Mendoza have plenty to prove when Cleveland hosts Las Vegas on Sunday night.
teamStories.detailText: BEREA, Ohio -- — Deshaun Watson and Fernando Mendoza have plenty to prove when Cleveland hosts Las Vegas on Sunday night. Watson will make his first Sunday night start since 2019, while the Browns are making their first “Sunday Night Football” appearance since 2021. Mendoza, the top overall pick in April's draft, will make his third NFL start and his first in primetime. Even though the Browns (6-4) are getting a national stage to show how much progress they have made in Todd Monken's first season as coach, Watson is trying to keep the same approach. “It’s still a game, just a time difference, but preparation still stays the same,” Watson said. "I think overall, it just gives us, and this organization, all the great things that we’ve been doing, that they wanted to flex us and put us on primetime. So overall, as an organization, as a team, definitely a great look.” Watson’s six fourth-quarter game-winning drives are tied with Denver's Bo Nix for the most in the league this season. The 10-year veteran has passed for at least 300 yards in his last three starts while the offense has started to open up more. “I feel like mentally, physically, my shoulder, my Achilles, me running the ball, trusting myself, making certain throws, the pressure situations, everything." Watson said about areas where he has improved. “Just each week, want to continue to get better.” Cleveland will try to go 5-0 at home for the first time since 1957, when Jim Brown was a rookie running back. It also has a six-game winning streak in home primetime games, including a 27-24 victory over Pittsburgh in Week 4. The Browns currently hold the sixth seed in the AFC, but New England is only one game back. They have not fared well though against rookie quarterbacks, going an NFL-worst 13-26 since their return to Cleveland in 1999. Rookie first-round QBs have a 19-8 mark and won the past five. Mendoza is the 20th quarterback selected first overall since the common draft started in 1966 to lose his first two starts. Five went on to win their third start, including noted Raiders bust JaMarcus Russell. Mendoza passed for 267 yards and three touchdowns in last week's 38-24 loss to Denver, but he completed only 18 of 37 passes and had a pick-6 in the fourth quarter when the Raiders were down by only seven points. “There’s still a long way to go, but I can tell you from the first snap against the Seahawks to the last snap of the Broncos game, I did feel more confident,” Mendoza said. “It’s hard to point out a specific aspect of the game that I feel like I’ve grown a lot in. However, I’ve seen a lot of points of improvement and I’m excited to play in Cleveland this week to try to improve on those and the rest of the season.” Las Vegas (4-7) is trying to avoid a fifth straight losing season, but has dropped its last three and seven of eight after a 3-0 start. Need to know Las Vegas (4-7) at Cleveland (6-4) When/where to watch: Sunday, 8:20 p.m. EST, NBC. Latest odds: Browns by 4 1/2. Against the spread: Raiders 6-5; Cleveland 7-3. Last week: Raiders lost to Broncos 38-24; Browns had a bye. Last meeting: Browns beat Raiders 24-10 on Nov. 23, 2025, in Las Vegas. Series record: Raiders lead 18-11 Matchup to watch Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty vs. Browns LB Quincy Williams . Jeanty leads NFL running backs with 507 yards receiving and is second with 51 receptions. Williams has been effective in pass coverage when being matched up against running backs. The Browns' biggest concern is making sure Jeanty doesn't find any open space like last week against Denver when he got separation on a wheel route and went 68 yards for a touchdown, including 47 yards after the catch. Stats and stuff — The Raiders have won five of the past six in the series, including the last three played in Cleveland. — Las Vegas allows 29.7 points per game, last in the NFL and putting the Raiders on pace for their third-worst scoring defense. The 1961 Oakland Raiders gave up a 32.7-point average and the 2020 Las Vegas Raiders allowed 29.9. The Raiders have given up 30 or more points in seven of the past eight weeks. — Cleveland and Tennessee (1-9) are the only teams to have been tied or trailing in the fourth quarter of every game this season. The last time the Browns did that was 2017, when they finished 0-16. — Raiders TE Brock Bowers needs 33 yards to pass Kellen Winslow and has the most yards receiving (2,583) by a non-receiver through his first 38 career games in league history. — Las Vegas DE Maxx Crosby is first in tackles for loss (142), quarterback hits (186) and is second in sacks (74 1/2) and quarterback pressures (503) among defensive linemen since entering the league in 2019. He had a career high five tackles for loss in last year's game. — Browns WR Denzel Boston leads NFL rookies in receiving yards (523) and tied for first with three receiving touchdowns. Four of his 33 receptions have been for at least 40 yards. WR KC Concepcion Jr. leads NFL rookies with 40 receptions and is third in receiving yards with 458. — Cleveland TE Harold Fannin Jr .'s 544 yards receiving are sixth among NFL tight ends and his 376 yards after the catch are second. — Browns CB Denzel Ward has tied a career high with three interceptions this season. His 116 passes defensed are second-most among active NFL players. ------ AP Sports Writer Mark Anderson in Las Vegas contributed to this report. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here
